articles.title: Incêndios destroem casas e plantação de cacau em Altamira, no PA | G1
articles.standfirst: Chamas atingiram área urbana e comunidade ribeirinha na Reserva Extrativista Riozinho do Anfrísio, a 450 km da cidade. Moradores perderam todos os pertences e pedem doações.
articles.summary: Chamas atingiram área urbana e comunidade ribeirinha na Reserva Extrativista Riozinho do Anfrísio, a 450 km da cidade. Moradores perderam todos os pertences e pedem doações.
articles.body:
Uma série de incêndios provocou destruição em diferentes pontos de Altamira , no sudoeste do Pará. As ocorrências, registradas tanto na área urbana quanto na zona ribeirinha do município, deixaram famílias desalojadas, destruíram residências e consumiram plantações agrícolas. O período de forte estiagem na região tem agravado a propagação do fogo.

Na área urbana de Altamira, um incêndio destruiu duas casas interligadas no Bairro Brasília. Ao todo, 10 pessoas de duas famílias, entre elas três crianças, ficaram desabrigadas.

O fogo teria começado na cozinha de uma das residências, que era de alvenaria. Em poucos minutos, as chamas se alastraram para a estrutura vizinha, construída em madeira. Ambas as casas eram alugadas.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado e agiu rapidamente para conter o avanço do fogo, evitando que outras residências do quarteirão fossem atingidas. As causas do início do incêndio ainda estão sendo investigadas.

A dona de casa Maria de Fátima Rodrigues Araújo, de 61 anos, relatou o desespero para salvar a família. Ela, que sobrevive da coleta de latinhas e da venda de amendoins, conseguiu retirar todos de casa a tempo. Ninguém ficou ferido.

"Só tive tempo de salvar minha família", desabafou a moradora.

Uma equipe da Secretaria Municipal de Assistência Social realizou o primeiro atendimento aos atingidos. Provisoriamente, as famílias estão abrigadas em casas de parentes.

Como perderam todos os documentos, roupas e móveis, os sobreviventes agora contam com a solidariedade da população para recomeçar e precisam de doações de mantimentos e itens básicos.

A destruição também alcançou a zona rural de Altamira. Na comunidade ribeirinha Boa Saúde, localizada na Reserva Extrativista (Resex) Riozinho do Anfrísio, a cerca de 450 km da sede do município, um incêndio de rápida propagação devastou a localidade.

De acordo com os moradores, o fogo começou em uma área de cultivo de cacau. Devido ao tempo seco e à vegetação vulnerável pela seca, as chamas se espalharam rapidamente, destruindo mais de 6 mil pés de cacau.

O incêndio atingiu a área residencial da comunidade. Seis casas cobertas de palha foram completamente consumidas pelo fogo.

Diante da velocidade do fogo, os ribeirinhos não conseguiram resgatar pertences pessoais e perderam tudo. Sem moradia e sem a principal fonte de renda (a lavoura de cacau), a comunidade faz um apelo por ajuda humanitária e doações para a reconstrução das moradias.

Ainda no perímetro urbano de Altamira, outra ocorrência mobilizou os bombeiros no entorno do Bairro Laranjeiras. O fogo atingiu uma área de vegetação rasteira, gerando fumaça e preocupação entre os moradores próximos.

A equipe de combate a incêndios conseguiu controlar as chamas antes que ganhassem maiores proporções ou chegassem perto das residências. Neste caso, não houve registro de feridos ou de danos materiais a imóveis.

articles.title: Resgate de Border Collie preso entre galpões dura 4 horas em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Bombeiros precisaram abrir uma parede de concreto para alcançar o animal, que foi retirado com vida e sem ferimentos aparentes.
articles.summary: Bombeiros de Ilhota abriram uma parede de concreto para concluir o resgate de Border Collie preso entre galpões por mais de quatro horas.
articles.body:
Um cachorro de médio porte, da raça Border Collie , ficou preso entre dois galpões de tecidos e foi resgatado pelo Corpo de Bombeiros Voluntários de Ilhota , no Vale do Itajaí , na quarta-feira (7).

A operação de resgate durou mais de quatro horas . Um vídeo mostra o momento em que o animal é retirado do local (veja abaixo) .

🐶 No vídeo, é possível ouvir o cachorro ganindo enquanto aguardava o resgate. As imagens também mostram o momento em que ele é retirado do local com vida, sem ferimentos aparentes, e entregue à dona.

Segundo a corporação, o cão passou por uma a bertura entre os galpões, caiu em um vão e ficou preso. O caso ocorreu na Rua Leoberto Leal, no Centro, por volta das 16h35.

Um cachorro preso entre dois galpões de armazenamento de tecidos e precisou ser resgatado pelos bombeiros — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros Voluntários de Ilhota

Os bombeiros tiveram dificuldade para acessar o local diretamente. Após avaliar a situação, a equipe decidiu entrar por um galpão que fica abaixo do ponto onde o cão estava preso.

Para alcançar o animal, os socorristas retiraram caixas que bloqueavam a passagem e abriram um buraco na parede de concreto. O corte na estrutura foi feito de forma controlada, com ferramentas adequadas.

Os trabalhos duraram cerca de 4 horas e 25 minutos , com a participação de nove bombeiros voluntários.

O cachorro foi resgatado com vida, sem ferimentos aparentes, e entregue à dona .

De acordo com os bombeiros, a operação priorizou a integridade do animal e a segurança dos socorristas.

articles.title: Santos ganha escola gratuita de cinema; inscrições começam em 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Escola Popular de Cinema Glauber Rocha é voltada a moradores das periferias da Baixada Santista e pretende produzir dois filmes por ano.
articles.summary: Escola Popular de Cinema Glauber Rocha é voltada a moradores das periferias da Baixada Santista e pretende produzir dois filmes por ano.
articles.body:
Arte no Dique inaugura Escola Popular de Cinema Glauber Rocha com presença de Pedro Paulo Rocha — Foto: Divulgação

A Escola Popular de Cinema Glauber Rocha foi inaugurada na noite desta quinta-feira (8), no Dique da Vila Gilda, na Zona Noroeste de Santos, no litoral de São Paulo. O espaço vai oferecer cursos gratuitos de audiovisual a moradores das periferias da Baixada Santista, com formação de dez meses.

As inscrições começam em 2027. O número de vagas e o calendário ainda não foram divulgados.

A inauguração ocorreu na sede do Instituto Arte no Dique e contou com a presença de Pedro Paulo Rocha, filho do cineasta Glauber Rocha, um dos principais nomes do Cinema Novo. A proposta é formar novos profissionais e ampliar o acesso de moradores das periferias ao mercado audiovisual.

Inscrições Início: 2027 Público: moradores das periferias da Baixada Santista Curso: gratuito Duração: dez meses Número de vagas: ainda não divulgado Calendário: ainda não divulgado

O curso será livre e gratuito, com disciplinas de Teoria e História do Cinema, Roteiro, Direção, Fotografia, Produção, Som, Montagem, Direção de Arte e Comunicação.

As aulas serão ministradas por profissionais que atuam no mercado de Santos e de São Paulo. A escola terá câmeras, equipamentos de iluminação e captação de som, além de computadores para montagem e edição. A estrutura foi adquirida com recursos de emenda parlamentar destinados à implantação do projeto.

A proposta é que os estudantes participem de todas as etapas da produção audiovisual, da criação do roteiro à gravação, montagem e divulgação. A escola também pretende incentivar os alunos a desenvolver histórias inspiradas nas próprias experiências e na realidade das comunidades onde vivem.

Segundo a coordenação, a expectativa é que os alunos produzam dois filmes ao fim de cada ano.

O Instituto Arte no Dique pretende inscrever os filmes produzidos pelos alunos em mostras e festivais nacionais e internacionais.

A instituição também trabalha na construção de uma parceria na França para ampliar o intercâmbio e criar oportunidades aos estudantes.

Glauber Rocha nasceu em Vitória da Conquista, na Bahia, em 1939, e se tornou um dos principais nomes do Cinema Novo, movimento que marcou o cinema brasileiro a partir dos anos 1960.

Entre seus filmes mais conhecidos estão "Deus e o Diabo na Terra do Sol", "Terra em Transe" e "Barravento", seu primeiro longa-metragem.

Antes de consolidar a carreira no cinema, Glauber estudou Direito na Bahia, participou do movimento estudantil e trabalhou como crítico de cinema. Dirigiu os curtas "O Pátio", em 1959, e "Cruz na Praça", em 1960, antes de lançar "Barravento", em 1962.

articles.title: Posada em Belém: Artista indígena faz show no Baile Felina | G1
articles.standfirst: Com raízes colombianas, compositora e DJ leva ao Baile Felina repertório que reúne carimbó, côco, cumbia, reggae, dancehall, hip hop e música eletrônica. Show será no sábado (10), na Casa Apoena.
articles.summary: A artista indígena Posada apresenta o álbum Flecha Envenenada no Baile Felina, na Casa Apoena, unindo ritmos da Amazônia e da América Latina no Círio de Nazaré.
articles.body:
Entre ritmos da Amazônia e da América Latina, artista indígena Posada apresenta show em Belém — Foto: Divulgação

Carimbó, cumbia, reggae, dancehall e música eletrônica atravessam o repertório que a artista indígena Posada apresenta em Belém no dia 10 de outubro, na Casa Apoena, no bairro da Cidade Velha. Com raízes familiares colombianas, a compositora, DJ e produtora sobe ao palco com “Flecha Envenenada”, seu álbum de estreia, lançado em março. O show integra a edição de Círio de Nazaré do Baile Felina, festa idealizada pelas DJs e produtoras culturais Nat/Esquema e Gabi Matos.

Nas oito faixas do disco, Posada reúne referências construídas em uma trajetória entre o Sul e o Norte do Brasil e em uma pesquisa sobre ancestralidade, identidade e os territórios de onde vieram seus antepassados. Belém ocupa um lugar importante nessa formação. A artista passou temporadas na cidade durante a juventude e encontrou aqui uma relação com a música que ultrapassava as casas e ocupava as ruas.

Para Posada, apresentar o álbum durante o Círio tem um significado particular. “O Círio é um momento muito importante no calendário e na vida do paraense. É um momento em que a cidade está muito viva, de fé, de afeto, de acolhimento e comunhão, mas também de liberdade. O Círio abraça todas as culturas, todas as religiões. É um momento de muita diversidade, de muita pluralidade”, afirma.

Artista indígena em contexto urbano, ela relaciona a criação musical aos próprios processos de retomada de identidade. A ideia atravessa o título do disco, que parte da imagem da flecha como instrumento de proteção.

“A flecha envenenada vem na representação de um artefato que está protegendo um território, que está protegendo uma história. Então, para mim, trazer as sonoridades que, a partir da minha experiência, sobrevivi nesses lugares é uma forma de proteger essas memórias”, explica.

A relação com a Colômbia passa pelas lembranças musicais do pai. Posada conta que cresceu ouvindo bolero e salsa e, ao longo da própria trajetória, identificou conexões entre essas referências e os sons encontrados no Pará. A cumbia e outras sonoridades latino-americanas também passaram a integrar uma pesquisa musical iniciada antes do álbum.

No Pará, algumas das experiências que marcaram essa formação vieram das temporadas em Belém. Posada lembra especialmente das viagens durante o Natal e o Ano Novo, quando a família se reunia na Matinha, área que hoje integra o bairro de Fátima. As festas se estendiam às ruas, com diferentes famílias colocando seus sistemas de som e DJs do lado de fora das casas.

“A cultura de estar na rua, de ocupar a rua com música, com festas, celebrações, foi uma experiência muito valiosa e que mudou muito também a minha forma de manifestação artística, popular”, conta.

Belém também atravessa o disco. “Tenoné”, faixa que abre o álbum em ritmo de côco, nasceu das histórias sobre a infância da mãe de Posada no bairro que dá nome à canção, entre igarapés, noites e brincadeiras.

Em “Madrugada”, são as experiências da própria artista que conduzem a narrativa. A segunda faixa do álbum, que dialoga com reggae, dancehall, rap e música eletrônica, ganhou um clipe dirigido por Guima Neto, realizado sem uma produtora responsável e com financiamento por meio de edital da Política Nacional Aldir Blanc (PNAB).

No vídeo, Posada percorre de bicicleta lugares relacionados à adolescência em Belém. O trajeto passa pela Matinha, São Brás, Nando Vinil e Feira do Açaí até chegar às margens do rio Guamá. “É alguém que está retornando à cidade e quer viver esse dia”, resume a artista.

“Flecha Envenenada”, álbum de estreia de Posada, lançado este ano. — Foto: Divulgação

O show integra a edição de Círio de Nazaré do Baile Felina, projeto idealizado por Nat/Esquema e Gabi Matos que busca ampliar a presença e a visibilidade de mulheres DJs no Pará. Para Posada, a apresentação representa também a continuidade de uma relação artística construída desde 2024, quando dividiu uma programação musical com as parceiras.

“São parceiras que estão totalmente conectadas com os movimentos que eu faço. A gente se conheceu tocando juntas em um line-up em 2024 e, a partir daí, seguiu sempre se acompanhando. Foram encontros que aconteceram de maneira muito orgânica. Tem toda uma construção por trás”, conta.

A possibilidade de apresentar “Flecha Envenenada” no Baile Felina já havia sido discutida anteriormente, mas não se concretizou por questões de agenda. “Estou muito animada, muito feliz e me preparando muito para esse momento de conexão e celebração”, afirma.

Nascida e criada em Belém, Nat/Esquema é pesquisadora, DJ, produtora cultural e curadora. Sua pesquisa musical percorre diferentes épocas e estilos, com atenção à música brasileira e paraense e à cultura dos discos de vinil no estado. Ela também integra a programação da noite.

articles.title: Sífilis em Teresina: 233 casos em gestantes e bebês até outubro | G1
articles.standfirst: Sem tratamento, a infecção pode provocar complicações como parto prematuro e lesões.
articles.summary: Teresina registrou 233 casos de sífilis em gestantes e bebês até outubro, com testes rápidos e tratamento gratuito disponíveis em toda a rede municipal de saúde.
articles.body:
Gravidez, mulher grávida. — Foto: Reprodução/DPESP

Teresina registrou 233 casos de sífilis em gestantes e bebês até 6 de outubro deste ano, segundo a Fundação Municipal de Saúde (FMS). Do total, 175 diagnósticos ocorreram em grávidas e 58 foram de sífilis congênita, transmitida da mãe para o filho .

Os números são menores que os registrados em 2025, quando a capital contabilizou 308 casos de sífilis em gestantes e 87 em bebês.

🔍 A sífilis é uma infecção bacteriana transmitida principalmente por relações sexuais sem preservativo. A doença também pode ser passada da mãe para o bebê durante a gestação ou no momento do parto.

De acordo com a FMS, um dos desafios no combate à doença é o fato de ela poder não apresentar sintomas nos estágios iniciais.

Por isso, a recomendação é que pessoas sexualmente ativas realizem testes regularmente para identificar a infecção e iniciar o tratamento o quanto antes .

Em gestantes, a doença está associada a riscos como parto prematuro, natimortalidade e sífilis congênita.

Em fases mais avançadas, também pode causar lesões na pele, nos ossos, além de problemas cardiovasculares e neurológicos.

articles.title: Lagoa Santa confirma 178 casos de sarna em meio à suspensão de aulas | G1
articles.standfirst: Outros 75 casos estão sob investigação no município, totalizando 253 notificações. Apenas nas últimas 24 horas, foram registradas 12 novas ocorrências.
articles.summary: Outros 75 casos estão sob investigação no município, totalizando 253 notificações. Apenas nas últimas 24 horas, foram registradas 12 novas ocorrências.
articles.body:
Lagoa Santa, na Grande BH, tem 178 casos confirmados de escabiose, também conhecida como sarna humana, nesta quinta-feira (8). Desde a manhã, as aulas em todas as escolas da rede municipal estão suspensas devido a um surto da doença .

Segundo o último boletim divulgado pela prefeitura, outros 75 casos estão em investigação no município, totalizando 253 notificações . Apenas nas últimas 24 horas, foram registradas 12 novas ocorrências.

Conforme a administração municipal, os registros de escabiose chegaram via hospital, Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBS) e escolas ( leia mais abaixo sobre a suspensão das aulas ).

"Todos os casos notificados foram direcionados para atendimento na rede municipal de saúde, com avaliação e indicação do tratamento adequado", afirmou a prefeitura.

O município também informou que as secretarias de Saúde e de Educação estão trabalhando juntas para acompanhar a situação epidemiológica da doença.

As aulas em todas as escolas municipais de Lagoa Santa, na Grande BH, foram suspensas entre quinta e sexta-feira (9) por causa do surto de sarna humana. A paralisação das atividades escolares foi anunciada pela prefeitura após pedidos de pais e responsáveis preocupados com o avanço da doença.

Em nota, a administração municipal afirmou que a suspensão foi adotada como medida adicional de precaução. No entanto, ressaltou que o fechamento das escolas não é uma recomendação técnica de rotina para o controle da escabiose e, sozinho, não interrompe a transmissão.

"O sucesso dessa medida depende diretamente da atuação das famílias durante o período em que as crianças permanecerão em casa", destacou a prefeitura.

Entre o fim de setembro e início de outubro, o g1 mostrou que uma escola municipal de Lagoa Santa havia suspendido as atividades após registrar 20 casos confirmados de sarna . Naquele momento, outro caso fora da instituição também estava confirmado.

O que é sarna e como prevenir a transmissão?

A escabiose é uma doença de pele causada por um ácaro que provoca coceira intensa e lesões. Segundo a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Lagoa Santa, a transmissão ocorre principalmente pelo contato direto e prolongado com a pele de uma pessoa infectada e, com menor frequência, pelo compartilhamento de roupas, toalhas e roupas de cama.

A doença não está relacionada à falta de higiene pessoal e não é transmitida por tosse ou espirro.

A orientação é procurar uma unidade de saúde diante de sintomas e seguir o tratamento prescrito. Familiares e contatos próximos devem realizar o tratamento ao mesmo tempo quando houver indicação da equipe de saúde.

Não há recomendação de medicação preventiva indiscriminada para toda a população. O retorno da criança às atividades escolares deve seguir a orientação dos profissionais de saúde, considerando o tratamento realizado e a situação individual.

Além do tratamento, a prefeitura recomenda os seguintes cuidados em casa:

Lavar roupas, toalhas e roupas de cama utilizadas no período relacionado ao início do tratamento. Quando possível, usar água quente, secar completamente e passar com ferro quente.

Guardar objetos que não possam ser lavados em um saco plástico bem fechado e deixá-los sem uso por sete dias.

Não compartilhar roupas, toalhas, lençóis, cobertores, travesseiros e outros objetos que tenham contato direto com a pele.

Manter a limpeza habitual da casa e, quando possível, aspirar sofás, colchões e tapetes. Não é necessário descartar móveis ou colchões.

Manter as unhas curtas e limpas e evitar coçar as lesões, para reduzir o risco de feridas e infecções.

Evitar contato prolongado de pele com pele até que o tratamento recomendado tenha sido realizado.

Não usar nem compartilhar medicamentos por conta própria.

Segundo a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde, a coceira pode persistir por algumas semanas mesmo após o tratamento adequado. Se surgirem novas lesões, piora da coceira, feridas com secreção, dor, febre ou sintomas em outros familiares, a orientação é procurar novamente uma unidade de saúde.

articles.title: Trânsito em Aracaju: Procissão causa bloqueios nesta segunda (12) | G1
articles.standfirst: Interdições acontecem na próxima segunda-feira (12), das 8h às 12h.
articles.summary: O trânsito em Aracaju terá interdições temporárias na segunda-feira (12), das 8h às 12h, devido à procissão de Nossa Senhora Aparecida entre os bairros Siqueira Campos e Bugio.
articles.body:
SMTT durante procissão no bairro São José — Foto: SMTT/arquivo

Na próxima segunda-feira (12), dia da Peregrinação do Dozenário e Festa de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, haverá bloqueios temporários no trânsito de Aracaju , das 8h às 12h.

Segundo a Superintendência Municipal de Transportes e Trânsito (SMTT), as interdições ocorrem em vias do bairro Siqueira Campos, passando por outros pontos da cidade até o bairro Bugio, onde a procissão será encerrada, na Praça Vereador Osvaldo Mendonça, em frente ao Santuário Nossa Senhora Aparecida.

A operação contará com 18 agentes de trânsito, três viaturas e 10 motocicletas. As equipes estarão distribuídas ao longo do percurso para realizar os bloqueios, orientar os condutores e organizar a circulação de veículos à medida que a procissão avançar.

A concentração será na Praça Dom José Tomaz, no bairro Siqueira Campos. De lá, os fiéis seguirão pela Rua Neópolis (contramão), Rua Alagoas, Rua Simeão Aguiar, Avenida São Paulo, Avenida Santa Gleide (contramão), Rua Radialista Silva Lima (contramão), Avenida Centenário, pela esquerda, no sentido da Rótula da Imagem, e Avenida Poço de Mero, até a Praça Vereador Osvaldo Mendonça.

A orientação aos condutores é evitar as áreas do trajeto, utilizar rotas alternativas, como a Avenida Chanceler Osvaldo Aranha, e redobrar a atenção durante o período da operação.

articles.title: 20 mil protestam em Madri após morte de idosa despejada | G1
articles.standfirst: Maricarmen Abascal, de 87 anos, morreu duas semanas após ser retirada do imóvel onde vivia havia 71 anos. Caso mobilizou manifestações em outras cidades da Espanha.
articles.summary: Cerca de 20 mil pessoas protestaram em Madri após a morte de Maricarmen Abascal, de 87 anos, despejada da casa onde vivia havia 71 anos.
articles.body:
Manifestantes marcham da praça Puerta del Sol, em Madri, onde estão acampados há dias, até o prédio onde vivia Maricarmen Abascal, de 87 anos, que morreu após ser despejada. O caso dela deu início a protestos por moradia na Espanha. — Foto: Susana Vera / Reuters

Cerca de 20 mil pessoas participaram nesta quinta-feira (8) de uma manifestação em memória de Maricarmen Abascal , de 87 anos, em Madri, na Espanha. A idosa morreu na última quarta (7), duas semanas depois de ser despejada da casa onde vivia havia 71 anos .

A manifestação foi organizada pelo Sindicato de Inquilinos e começou às 20h na Puerta del Sol, no centro da capital espanhola. Flores, velas e mensagens foram deixadas durante o dia no local onde os manifestantes se reuniram.

O grupo seguiu em direção à rua Sainz de Baranda, onde Maricarmen morava desde os 17 anos. Ela foi retirada do imóvel em 23 de setembro , depois que a empresa imobiliária Urbagestión comprou o prédio e passou a cobrar € 2.650 de aluguel por mês. Maricarmen recebia uma aposentadoria de cerca de € 1.350.

Após o despejo, ela foi internada no Hospital Gregorio Marañón. Segundo o Sindicato de Inquilinos, a internação ocorreu após o desgaste provocado pelo processo de despejo.

Na passagem pela praça de Cibeles, onde fica a sede da Prefeitura de Madri, os manifestantes fizeram um minuto de silêncio. O grupo também lembrou o caso de Olga, uma mulher que morreu recentemente após ser retirada de sua casa em L'Hospitalet, na região de Barcelona.

Cartazes exibiam frases como "O rentismo mata" e "Maricarmen somos todas".

A manifestação em Madri fez parte de uma série de atos realizados nesta quinta-feira em outras cidades espanholas. Houve concentrações e vigílias em Barcelona, Valência, Zaragoza e Sevilha, organizadas por grupos que defendem mudanças nas políticas de moradia.

Durante o ato em Madri, uma coroa de flores foi colocada em homenagem a Maricarmen. Uma faixa dizia que ela deveria ser lembrada na luta pelo direito à moradia.

O Sindicato de Inquilinos convocou uma greve geral para 11 de novembro e também passou a defender o adiantamento das eleições gerais.

articles.title: BR-116 será interditada para içamento de pórtico de pedágio | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a concessionária Ecovias das Gerais, os trabalhos serão realizados no km 313 da rodovia.
articles.summary: Segundo a concessionária Ecovias das Gerais, os trabalhos serão realizados no km 313 da rodovia.
articles.body:
Içamento de pórtico de pedágio — Foto: Ecovias das Gerais

O trânsito será totalmente interditado na BR-116, em Itambacuri , para o içamento de um pórtico de pedágio eletrônico nesta sexta-feira (9).

Segundo a concessionária Ecovias das Gerais, os trabalhos serão realizados no km 313 da rodovia.

A pista será parcialmente fechada a partir das 8h. Em seguida, às 10h, haverá a interdição total. A estimativa é que o trânsito seja liberado às 12h.

A BR-116 terá pedágio sem cabines e sem cancelas . Segundo a concessionária que administra o trecho mineiro da rodovia, o modelo, chamado free flow, faz a cobrança eletronicamente por meio de equipamentos instalados sobre a pista, capazes de identificar os veículos em movimento e registrar a passagem automaticamente.

A tecnologia substitui as tradicionais praças de pedágio por pórticos equipados com câmeras e sensores, capazes de identificar os veículos em movimento e realizar a cobrança sem necessidade de parada.

No sistema, a identificação dos veículos ocorre por meio de uma tag eletrônica instalada no para-brisa ou pela leitura da placa por câmeras de reconhecimento óptico de caracteres (OCR). Os sensores também classificam os veículos conforme a altura, a largura, o comprimento e o número de eixos, garantindo a cobrança da tarifa correspondente à categoria.

De acordo com a concessionária, a tecnologia já é utilizada em mais de 20 países, entre eles Estados Unidos e Chile, e vem sendo adotada em novas concessões rodoviárias brasileiras, em estados como São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais e Rio Grande do Sul.

Segundo a Ecovias, entre as principais vantagens do sistema estão:

Redução de frenagens e acelerações, o que pode contribuir para a diminuição do consumo de combustível e da emissão de poluentes;

Aumento da segurança viária, com a redução do risco de acidentes próximos aos pontos de cobrança.

O início da cobrança está previsto para dezembro de 2026. No entanto, ainda não há uma data oficial, pois a entrada em operação depende das etapas de implantação e da decisão da Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT).

Quando a data for publicada no Diário Oficial, a concessionária informou que fará ampla divulgação antecipadamente.

Motoristas que possuem tag eletrônica terão a cobrança realizada automaticamente no momento da passagem pelo pórtico, sem necessidade de qualquer ação adicional. Além da praticidade, a modalidade garante desconto de 5% sobre o valor da tarifa e permite acesso ao Desconto para Usuários Frequentes (DUF).

Já os condutores que não possuem tag ou que estiverem com o dispositivo inativo terão o veículo identificado pela placa.

Nesses casos, o pagamento poderá ser feito em até 30 dias após a passagem pela internet ou em totens de autoatendimento que serão instalados nos Serviços de Atendimento ao Usuário (SAUs). Ao longo do trecho concessionado, serão disponibilizados 14 pontos de atendimento.

articles.title: Mulher retira crianças antes de desabamento em Bom Jesus do Itabapoana | G1
articles.standfirst: Estrutura caiu no distrito de Usina Santa Isabel; seis pessoas estavam no imóvel. Ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.summary: Estrutura caiu no distrito de Usina Santa Isabel; seis pessoas estavam no imóvel e ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.body:
Uma casa desabou na tarde desta quinta-feira (8), na Rua da Serralheria, no distrito de Usina Santa Isabel, em Bom Jesus do Itabapoana, no Noroeste Fluminense.

Uma mulher que estava no imóvel percebeu que o muro estava balançando e conseguiu retirar quatro crianças, que seriam seus netos, e outra mulher antes que a estrutura desabasse.

De acordo com Fábio Mello, secretário de Defesa Civil de Bom Jesus do Itabapoana, a casa ficou bastante danificada. Segundo ele, equipes foram acionadas e, ao chegarem ao local, encontraram duas mulheres e quatro crianças no imóvel. Ninguém ficou ferido. O local, até então, não apresentava risco.

"Os moradores já estão sendo atendidos pela Assistência Social para dar andamento ao processo de aluguel social", informa o secretário.

Ainda de acordo com a Defesa Civil, as duas mulheres e as quatro crianças foram encaminhadas para atendimento no Centro de Referência Especializado de Assistência Social (Creas).

A Defesa Civil realizou uma vistoria no local e constatou os danos causados pelo desabamento. A causa da queda ainda será avaliada.

Segundo ele, seis pessoas estavam no imóvel. O local, até então, não apresentava risco. — Foto: Alan Gonçalves

articles.title: Hurricane Isaias strengthens to Category 2 storm, evacuations expand across Gulf ahead of dangerous landfall
articles.summary: Hurricane Isaias is continuing to strengthen in the Gulf after becoming the first Atlantic hurricane of the season and is forecast to make landfall along the...
articles.body:
Three states, including Alabama, Florida and Georgia, have declared states of emergencies ahead of Hurricane Isaias.

Thousands of residents have been ordered to evacuate across two states.

Hurricane Isaias is currently a Category 2 storm and continues to strengthen in the Gulf.

Isaias is expected to approach the coast by Friday, with landfall currently estimated to be 11 p.m. EST between Gulf Shores, Alabama, and Pensacola, Florida.

Hurricane Isaias is continuing to strengthen in the Gulf after becoming the first Atlantic hurricane of the season and expected to make landfall along the northern Gulf Coast later this week as a dangerous Category 2 hurricane.

Isaias is expected to approach the coast by Friday, with landfall currently estimated to be sometime late Friday or early Saturday between Gulf Shores, Alabama, and Pensacola, Florida.

Isaias strengthened from a Category 1 to a Category 2 hurricane on Thursday, with sustained winds of 100 mph as it moves northeast at 12 mph.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey and Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp have declared states of emergency ahead of the storm.

In a Thursday press conference, DeSantis urged residents to prepare now, including filling up their gas tanks and stocking up on enough water and nonperishable food to last through a potential power outage.

"If you are in the Panhandle, assume that you are going to lose power," DeSantis said. "Prepare to lose power. That is likely to happen with a storm that is at hurricane status."

Over a dozen Florida and Alabama counties have canceled school through the end of the week, and multiple colleges have closed their campuses.

Meanwhile, evacuation orders have been issued for Dauphin Island in Alabama, as well as Okaloosa and Escambia counties in Florida.

Mandatory evacuation orders have also been issued in Walton County, Florida.

The City of Orange Beach has issued mandatory evacuations of coastal tourists and visitors.

"In anticipation of the expected impacts from Tropical Storm Isaias, the cities of Gulf Shores and Orange Beach are encouraging all non‑residents, and residents living in low-lying, flood prone areas to voluntarily evacuate," a statement from city officials said. "City officials urge all individuals who are not permanent residents to leave the area immediately and relocate to a safer location."

Both Shell and Chevron have instituted shut-in production procedures across five of their offshore oil facilities in the Gulf and removed non-essential workers, respectively.

BP said it was also removing non-essential personnel and securing offshore facilities. ExxonMobil operations are currently normal, but they are monitoring the forecast closely.

Hurricane Isaias strengthened from Tropical Storm Isaias late Wednesday night.

In their Wednesday 11 p.m. update, the National Hurricane Center kept Isaias at tropical storm strength. About 30 minutes later, they released a special advisory stating that Isaias had indeed strengthened into a Category 1 hurricane.

Isaias rapidly intensified from a tropical storm into a Category 1 hurricane, with winds increasing by 40 mph in just six hours between Wednesday afternoon and late Wednesday night.

Isaias' forecast cone shows it heading directly toward the northern Gulf Coast, with impacts centered over roughly 30 million people in Louisiana , Alabama , Mississippi and the Florida Panhandle.

Tropical weather advisories have expanded inland, across parts of southern Alabama and southwestern Georgia.

A Hurricane Warning is in effect from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the Bay/Gulf County Line in Florida.

A Storm Surge Warning is also in effect from the mouth of the Mississippi to the Suwannee River in Florida's Big Bend region.

"The combination of a dangerous storm surge and the tide will cause normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by rising waters moving inland from the shoreline," the NHC said.

Currently, between 5 and 7 feet of surge is forecast for Mobile Bay and from Ocean Springs, Mississippi , to Indian Pass, Florida.

Heavy rain is expected to begin on Friday, with flash flooding , damaging wind gusts, storm surge and even tornadoes possible as the storm comes ashore.

The storm is expected to continue to strengthen early Friday, with heavy rain reaching parts of the Gulf Coast as early as Friday morning.

FOX Weather Hurricane Specialist Bryan Norcross noted that several dynamic factors still remain at play, which will determine how strong and exactly where Isaias will make landfall, namely the storm's angle of approach and how the winds will impact the storm as it comes ashore.

Some forecast models show Isaias weakening at landfall, while others show the storm strengthening as strong winds high in the atmosphere interact with it from the north.

Norcross said most of the storm's most impactful weather will most likely be on the right side of the storm's center.

Meanwhile, Noaa 's Weather Prediction Center (WPC) has issued a Level 3 out of 4 flash flood risk for Mobile , Alabama, and the Florida Panhandle west of Panama City . A Level 2 risk includes Atlanta and Montgomery , Alabama, and eventually shifts inland into Saturday to include the Carolinas and Tennessee Valley.

" Rainfall estimates currently show 6 to 10 inches with localized higher amounts which will lead to flash and urban flooding and eventually river flooding," the FOX Forecast Center said.

NOAA's Storm Prediction Center (SPC) has issued a Level 2 out of 5 risk of severe weather for Saturday across southern Alabama and into the Florida Panhandle, with a particular threat of tornadoes as the storm's outer bands come ashore.

The system is expected to move inland quickly with heavy rain spreading across the Southeast Saturday, triggering a broad Level 2 flash flood risk from some places along the Mississippi River to the Southeast coast.

This story is developing. Check back frequently for updates.

articles.title: 'The View' co-host predicts Texas will 'go blue' as polls show Talarico leading Paxton
articles.summary: Sunny Hostin predicted Texas will go blue, citing polls showing James Talarico leading Ken Paxton among women, young voters and Hispanic voters.
articles.body: "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin predicted Thursday that voters will flip Texas blue in November for the first time in about 30 years as the panel discussed the tight race between Democratic candidate James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton for the U.S. Senate. "I think we will. I think we will see Texas go blue, actually. I really do," Hostin remarked. "In September, not only one, but eight pollsters had Talarico ahead 51-45%. That is so significant given that a Democrat hasn't won statewide office in 30 years. "That same poll showed that he is leading Paxton among women, 56% to 40%. Among voters aged 18 to 29, 66% to 22%, and among Hispanics, 62% to 30%. We're talking about Texas. He's going to win this race." TEXAS VOTERS HAVE PLENTY TO SAY ABOUT WHETHER LONE STAR STATE COULD TURN BLUE Co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin argued that Talarico's edge in the Lone Star State was a referendum on President Donald Trump's administration. "I mean, the fact that Texas is in play speaks to the moment right now that people are so frustrated with the current leadership," she said. "A Democrat hasn't won statewide in Texas in over 30 years. I still think it could go either direction for Paxton or Talarico, but this is kind of a perfect storm, and it's a mess of the president's own making." Griffin agreed the state might flip blue, calling Talarico a good candidate. She argued that Sen. John Cornyn would've been a better Republican candidate over Paxton, who was endorsed by Trump and came out on top in the GOP primary. A Fox News poll released in October found Talarico enjoying a net positive personal rating of 8 points among likely Texas voters (52% favorable vs. 44% unfavorable), compared to Paxton, who is underwater by 18 points (40% vs. 58%). Republicans are six times more likely to view Paxton unfavorably (32%) than Democrats do Talarico (5%). FOX NEWS POLL: GOP DIVISIONS SHAPE TEXAS SENATE RACE Likely Texas voters are split on control of the Senate: 49% prefer a Democratic Senate while 50% favor a Republican upper chamber. Eight percent of self-identified Republicans prefer the Democrats in power versus 1% of Democrats crossing over to pick the GOP. All this gives Talarico a slim 2-point edge over Paxton (51-49%) in the poll among likely voters. These matchup results are within the margin of sampling error. DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING. HERE ARE 3 FORCES THAT COULD STOP IT Co-hosts Whoopi Goldberg and Ana Navarro cast some doubt on the positive polling for the Democratic candidate. "Two-thousand sixteen left me scared," Navarro said. "I have hope. People should have hope, but hope alone won't win an election. People got to turn hope into vote. And I don't think they, you know, relying on polls and just kind of sitting back and getting complacent is something that nobody can afford to do if they want to see change." Paxton's campaign did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment. MEET THE VOTERS WHO COULD BREAK THE GOP’S DECADESLONG GRIP ON A REPUBLICAN STRONGHOLD Trump campaigned with Paxton in San Antonio, Texas, Wednesday. They both pointed to Talarico's absence from campaigning at the event. The Senate candidate's campaign responded to the criticism, explaining Talarico has been sick with the flu and is expected to return to the campaign trail this weekend. articles.title: Curtis Flowers, a Black man whose death sentence was tossed by Supreme Court, dies in Mississippi
articles.summary: Curtis Flowers, a Black man who spent more than 22 years in prison and was on death row in Mississippi before the U.S.
articles.body: Curtis Flowers, a Black man who spent more than 22 years in prison and was on death row in Mississippi before the U.S. Supreme Court threw out his conviction and death sentence, has died. He was 56. Flowers’ family confirmed that he died Wednesday at his home in Mississippi, attorney Rob McDuff told The Associated Press Thursday. No cause of death was given, said McDuff, who was part of Flowers’ legal team. Flowers was 26 when he was arrested several months after the July 1996 shooting deaths of four people inside a Winona, Mississippi, furniture store. At the time, prosecutors described him as a disgruntled former employee who sought revenge against the store’s owner because she fired him and withheld most of his pay to cover the cost of merchandise he damaged. Nearly $300 was found missing after the killings. Flowers was tried in the killings six times. Justice Brett Kavanaugh wrote in the high court’s 7-2 decision in 2019 that the removal of Black prospective jurors deprived Flowers of a fair trial. During the sixth trial in 2010, Flowers was sentenced to death. There were 11 white jurors and one Black juror who considered the case after District Attorney Doug Evans struck five Black prospective jurors. Flowers remained in prison for six months after the Supreme Court ruling because he was still under indictment. He finally was released in December 2019 after a judge set bond. Mississippi dropped charges against Flowers in September 2020. “Today, I am finally free from the injustice that left me locked in a box for nearly twenty three years,” Flowers said in a statement. “I’ve been asked if I ever thought this day would come. I have been blessed with a family that never gave up on me and with them by my side, I knew it would.” The legal team that represented Flowers for more than two decades said Thursday in a statement that each member feels “privileged to have called him a client.” “Later, in the years after his release and exoneration, we felt equally honored to call him a friend,” the legal team said. “No matter where he was — on death row, at home on his parents’ porch with his feet up, singing in church, or fishing in a local pond — Curtis shared his light.” The trials stretched back more than 20 years. The records showed Evans’ “relentless, determined effort to rid the jury of black individuals,” with the goal of an all-white jury, Kavanaugh wrote. In the earlier trials, three convictions were tossed out, including one when the prosecutor improperly excluded African Americans from the jury. In the second trial, the judge chided Evans for striking a juror based on race. Two other trials ended when jurors couldn’t reach unanimous verdicts. Kavanaugh noted that Evans had removed 41 of the 42 prospective Black jurors over the six trials. Flowers filed a lawsuit in 2021 against Evans and three investigators who worked with the district attorney. The suit claimed Evans and the investigators engaged in misconduct, including “pressuring witnesses to fabricate claims about seeing Mr. Flowers in particular locations on the day of the murders” and ignoring other possible suspects. Earlier that year, a judge ordered the state of Mississippi to pay Flowers $500,000 for wrongful imprisonment — the maximum under a state law that allows up to $50,000 a year for 10 years. Evans retired in 2023 after more than 30 years as district attorney. His jury selection tactics had been scrutinized for years. Flowers’ name is “etched into U.S. Supreme Court jurisprudence — about what it means to fight for a fair trial free from racial bias in the selection of jurors,” Flowers’ legal team said. “And also for that, but for so many other reasons, his name is etched into our memories, too — professional and personal. We will miss him.”

articles.title: An Arkansas family treated the same fence as its property line for nearly six decades; after new neighbours removed fencing and trees, an appeals court upheld $12,000 in treble damages and an order to rebuild the fence
articles.summary: A fence that had been treated as a property boundary since 1967 has been upheld as the dividing line between two Arkansas properties, after a dispute over
articles.body: A fence that had been treated as a property boundary since 1967 has been upheld as the dividing line between two Arkansas properties, after a dispute over trees and fencing reached the state Court of Appeals. The ruling in Floyd v. Bowlin-Lemon, reported by Justia, Leagle and Case Law Wire, affirmed the Bowlins’ boundary claim, a $12,000 treble-damages award and an order requiring the neighbouring owners to rebuild the fence. The case involved adjoining properties in Crawford County and centred on a fence line that the Bowlin family had treated as its southern boundary for decades. According to the Arkansas Court of Appeals, Joy Bowlin-Lemon’s family acquired the property in 1967. The family was shown the existing fence lines when it purchased the land and subsequently used those fences as practical boundaries. The property was used for livestock, including cattle and horses, while the family also maintained the land up to the fence by brush hogging and cutting hay.That arrangement remained unchallenged for decades. The dispute emerged after Ty Floyd, Kristy Floyd and Cottage Creations LLC acquired the neighbouring property. The court record says portions of the longstanding fence were removed beginning in 2017, with the fence eventually torn down. Trees in the disputed area were also cut down. The Bowlins eventually filed a lawsuit in 2023, alleging trespass and destruction of their fencing and trees. A Crawford County Circuit Court trial followed in October 2024.The fence became more than just a fenceThe central legal question was whether years of treating the fence as the boundary could establish a legally recognised boundary even if the fence did not precisely match the surveyed property line. The appeals court said yes.Under Arkansas law, a boundary by acquiescence can arise when neighbouring landowners tacitly accept a particular line as the dividing boundary for a long period. The court noted that an express agreement is not required, nor does there need to have been an earlier dispute over the property line.In this case, the decades of maintenance and use along the fence, combined with the absence of objections from neighbouring owners, provided sufficient evidence for the lower court’s decision. The court also noted that the southern fence extended roughly 30 to 40 feet beyond the surveyed property line. Despite that discrepancy, the long-established conduct surrounding the fence supported its recognition as the boundary.Tree removal resulted in $12,000 damagesThe dispute also became costly for the Floyds. The circuit court determined that the trees removed from the disputed area were worth $4,000. The Arkansas Court of Appeals upheld that valuation, finding that testimony about the number and type of trees, photographs of the property and evidence of the clearing provided enough support.The court also upheld treble damages, bringing the total award to $12,000. Arkansas law allows treble damages when someone cuts, destroys or removes trees belonging to another person. The appeals court found enough evidence to support the finding that the tree removal was intentional or, at minimum, sufficiently reckless or negligent to trigger the statute. Among the evidence considered was the presence of no-trespassing signs along the fence and Ty Floyd’s admission that he removed trees and portions of the fencing.The fence must be rebuiltThe lower court also ordered the Floyds to rebuild fencing along the eastern and southern boundaries. The appeals court left that order intact. It noted that Ty Floyd had indicated during the trial that he was willing to rebuild the fence, while his attorney did not object when the Bowlins requested the injunction.That meant the Floyds could not later challenge the fence-rebuilding requirement on appeal. There was, however, one issue the appeals court sent back to the circuit court. The original judgment did not contain a sufficiently precise legal description of the boundary. The appeals court therefore remanded the case for the limited purpose of adding a specific description that would allow the established boundary to be identified directly from the judgment.The decision underscores how decades of conduct can matter in property disputes. A fence may begin as a practical marker, but when generations of adjoining owners consistently treat it as the dividing line, that conduct can ultimately carry legal weight, even when a later survey points somewhere else.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir: High court orders passport revival for student purusing MBBS in Iran
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir High Court ordered Thursday revival of Kashmir student’s passport so that she can complete her MBBS in Iran.
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir High Court ordered Thursday revival of Kashmir student’s passport so that she can complete her MBBS in Iran.The authorities had impounded Ibra Khan’s passport based on a CID adverse report about an FIR against her father in 1997, although she was born in 2005. The report cited “aspersions” against Khan’s father in relation to the case and “apprehensions that she may join anti-India forces”.“This court has the highest concern towards the security of the country. In a very limited intervention and keeping in view that the appellant (student) has completed half her MBBS, we dispose of the appeal by directing that the passport be revived for the remaining period of her course,” a division bench of Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal said.Khan is pursuing MBBS at Tehran University of Medical Sciences. She was issued a passport in Oct 2024 but received showcause notices March 27, 2026 and April 9, 2026 from passport authorities over her father’s case before her passport was impounded on May 4, 2026.Khan moved the HC but a single-judge bench dismissed her petition saying it found no reason to interfere in the decision by authorities and citing an alternative remedy of appeal under Passports Act, 1967.Khan then approached the division bench. Her counsel Salih Pirzada argued that she began pursuing MBBS in 2024 but owing to the prevailing turmoil in the region, she returned to India. It was during this period that she received the notices, followed by the passport’s impounding without clear reasons.J&K’s additional advocate-general (AAG) cited the adverse CID report and claimed Khan had not replied to the show-cause notices, leaving authorities with no alternative but to impound the passport.Following this, the division bench of Justices Bhati and Nargal called for the CID report, which cited the case against Khan’s father and “apprehensions” about the security and sovereignty of the country.Khan’s counsel Pirzada contended that the state had not been able to pinpoint the reasons for such apprehensions given that the case against her father dated to 1997 whereas she herself was born eight years later.The division bench eventually allowed Khan’s appeal by ordering the passport’s revival, saying the authorities were free to impose conditions and directing her to comply with any such riders.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: FIRST ON FOX: FBI targets Ghana scam compound linked to nearly $10M in losses, more than 130 detained
articles.summary: The FBI's Operation Blackout led to over 130 arrests in Ghana and nearly $10 million in fraud losses tied to scam compounds targeting American seniors.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: The FBI's global crackdown on overseas scam centers targeting Americans has led to more than 130 arrests or detentions in Ghana, with investigators identifying nearly $10 million in financial losses, Fox News Digital has learned. The latest takedown is part of Operation Blackout, the FBI's international campaign to dismantle scam compounds that prey on Americans, particularly seniors. According to information provided to Fox News Digital by the FBI, investigators have identified 89 fraud victims and seized more than 300 devices. The more than 130 individuals arrested or detained include suspected trafficking victims expected to be repatriated to their home countries, primarily Nigeria. EXCLUSIVE: FBI EXTRADITIONS SOAR AS PATEL RAMPS UP FOREIGN OUTREACH, VOWS 'NO SANCTUARY' FBI Director Kash Patel said the operation reflects the bureau's broader effort to dismantle international fraud networks at their source. "The FBI’s 'Operation Blackout' is our historic, global scam center fraud demolition operation that takes apart scam compounds all over the world targeting American citizens – primarily seniors," Patel said. "We are attacking this problem right at the source and blowing these compounds up, seizing billions of dollars, freeing thousands of trafficked workers, and protecting tens of thousands of Americans at risk of looking their hard-earned savings through these scams. Those who steal from Americans no longer have sanctuary – this FBI will find them and bring them to justice." BURMA APPROVES DEATH PENALTY FOR SCAMMERS MONTHS AFTER FBI'S $8 BILLION CRYPTO CRACKDOWN The Ghana operation follows an earlier warning from Patel that international scam networks were expanding beyond Southeast Asia and the Middle East into Africa. "That’s why you’re seeing the migration of these scam compounds to central and sub-Saharan Africa, which is where we are already pre-positioned to take them off," Patel told Fox News Digital in September. That same month, U.S. investigators helped authorities in Madagascar dismantle 13 scam centers linked to Chinese organized crime syndicates, processing more than 3,200 electronic devices, according to previous Fox News Digital reporting. FBI SEIZES RECORD-SETTING $8 BILLION IN CRYPTOCURRENCY AMID INTERCONTINENTAL 'SCAM COMPOUND' CRACKDOWN The FBI says Operation Blackout has seized roughly $17 billion globally, led to hundreds of arrests and freed thousands of trafficked workers. The bureau has not provided a detailed breakdown of the seized assets. The bureau also says it has warned more than 10,000 Americans about suspected scams, preventing an estimated $670 million in financial losses. The FBI previously reported that 77% of the more than 10,400 potential victims contacted through its Operation Level Up prevention initiative did not realize they were being scammed. articles.title: Teen wearing helmet camera kills worker at Polish school amid fears of copycat attacks
articles.summary: A 15-year-old wearing a helmet camera allegedly killed a school employee and wounded two others in Poland's second school stabbing attack in two days.
articles.body: A 15-year-old boy wielding a knife and wearing a helmet-mounted camera attacked a Polish primary school he used to attend, allegedly killing one employee and wounding two others in the country's second school stabbing in two days. Authorities are investigating whether the attacks are connected to an online challenge encouraging teenagers to kill as many people as possible. Police said a 37-year-old woman who worked as a caretaker died in the Thursday morning attack at the school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, northeast of Warsaw. The school's head teacher, Krzysztof Ochmanski, was injured while subduing the teenager, officials said. Ochmanski told a radio station he heard a scream and ran into a hallway. MOTHER ACCUSED OF TRYING TO KILL DAUGHTERS IN FREEWAY CRASH AND KNIFE ATTACK AS SOLDIERS STEP IN "He wounded me with the blade of a rather long knife — he had three knives on him — and hit me with the handle," Ochmanski told the public broadcaster Polskie Radio RDC. "By then, I had managed to restrain him." The day before the latest attack, a 19-year-old allegedly wounded 10 people, including himself, at a school in Ostroleka, which is in northeastern Poland. Also this week, police arrested a 17-year-old in Sierpc in north-central Poland after authorities suspected he was planning a similar attack, Reuters reported. AMERICAN YOUTH RADICALIZED ONLINE, BUSTED IN SUSPECTED TERROR PLOTS AFTER HATING COUNTRY ON SOCIAL MEDIA "We fear a grim copycat phenomenon," Prime Minister Donald Tusk told an emergency meeting, according to Reuters. "We are facing an extraordinary situation. ... For the first time, we are dealing with a killer who wore a helmet-mounted camera, intending to film the knife attack." Tusk ordered police to visit schools every day to discourage further violence. "I mean, I didn't know if it was even real — I still don't know if it's true, actually — because it sounds so unreal, so terrifying, just like something out of a movie: some kind of challenge to kill as many people as possible," she said.

articles.title: AI is being used to steal school pictures, photographers warn
articles.summary: Ian Gilbert says he's heard parents boasting about using AI to take the watermark off his photos.
articles.body:
A photographer is warning parents who use artificial intelligence to take the watermark off school pictures about the dangers of how companies can use images of their children.

Ian Gilbert, founder of Emotion Picture Photography, said he had heard parents boasting at the school gates about how they use the tool to avoid paying for photos.

"The scary thing is when you submit a picture to AI by default it is allowed to do whatever it wants and I don't think a lot of parents realise that," he said.

An AI safety expert said he understood why people did it, and that it may seem harmless, but uploading any identifiable information, including photographs, was "not worth the risk".

Gilbert, from Pontypool, Torfaen, urged parents to think carefully before uploading their child's photograph to an AI tool.

Annual school photographs are a rite of passage but, with technology now able to remove watermarks from preview images in seconds, some parents are bypassing the payment process altogether.

"It is theft, it is shoplifting," said 47-year-old Gilbert.

"People wouldn't go into a shop and take a tag off something and take it without paying.

"It's as though because it's something you can do online at home, it seems to numb it in people's eyes."

Gilbert said other photographers were increasingly seeing the same behaviour from parents.

He noticed that about 25% of images sent out were being screenshot to be used in AI tools as he is notified when it happens.

"That's a quarter of parents not paying. A quarter of profit lost for us. Also the school get a cut from the revenue as well, so it's a loss for the school."

The photographer said he had noticed a drop in profits in the past 12 months.

He said he heard parents at the school gates talking using AI to avoid paying after he had been inside taking photos.

"They were referring to my own photos that I took at the school.

"One said 'Are you going to buy the pics?' And the other said 'I'm just going to get AI to remove the watermark off and it only costs me a pound'."

He said all people had to do was claim they were the owner of the image in order for the watermark to be removed.

Gilbert told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast that he wanted his photos to be affordable so charged from £9.

"For the sake of a couple of pounds with AI you're getting such a lower-quality product and ultimately it just makes us have to put prices up again, which is unfair for everyone," he said.

"You are constantly fighting and chasing your tail."

He added that the company he worked with was working to implement "high-tech methods to beat AI" including putting moving images over photos so they cannot be copied.

Dr Simon Thorne, a senior computer science lecturer at Cardiff School of Technologies, urged people, as a general rule, to "never upload any personable identifiable photos".

"It's a terrible idea. It's a big risk," he said.

"The dataset could get leaked online potentially and your material can be used to train future generations of the model. The image could be sold - you have no idea.

"Depending on the service, you may have very little idea how long that image is retained, how it is processed or whether it is reused."

Thorne said if the photograph contained other children, it raises an additional issue because their parents may have no idea that an image of their child has been uploaded to an AI system.

"We recently had a case where a child was ill and missed a school photograph, so a parent used AI to add them back into the picture afterwards," he said.

"I can understand entirely why they did that, but they did not seem to appreciate that uploading and manipulating images of children in this way can carry real privacy and safeguarding risks."

Theft aside, Gilbert said this method also gave people a low-quality photo.

"Our work is not just a quick shot - we have really beautiful set ups and spend a lot of time and money creating images.

"Across the board it's getting worse and worse and if it gets to the point where it's not profitable for us, I may have to stop my service."

"It's a huge issue, but I don't know how we would attack it. How would you make ChapGPT aware and hold them to account? It feels like a David and Goliath situation."

He added that the Guild of Photographers was looking at how they can bring prosecutions to people using such services and not paying.

Victoria Welton, a photographer based in Crewkerne, works across 15 schools and nurseries in Somerset.

She also said many parents were using AI to take the watermark off pictures so they could access them for free.

She added they were stealing photographers' livelihoods as well as possibly putting children at risk.

"To put your child's photograph through AI makes my blood boil. AI is a system we know nothing about. We don't know where the photo is going," she said.

Tessa Chapman, a photographer based in south Somerset, said parents removing watermarks were costing her a "huge amount of money".

She said: "It's illegal. It's our livelihoods. I think a lot of parents don't realise that.

"School photography is very historical. For some parents it's absolutely huge.

"What I noticed over the years is, often in lower socio-economic areas, this might be the only professional image that a family can afford of their child.

"I'm just trying to run a business. I have to have faith in people's honesty."

Dylan Evans, a 21-year-old sports photographer, had only been shooting for a few weeks when he noticed that people were using AI to remove his watermark from photos.

"It was just gutting. I only charge £2 a picture. I put all these hours in taking the photos and then I'm up until two o'clock in the morning editing all these photos, and I have a full-time job too."

Two years ago Evans, from Caersw, Powys, asked for a camera for Christmas and got in touch with his local football club about taking photos.

"It just started from there really. I went down most Saturdays and Sundays, taking photos of the players and then branched out to other clubs as well."

Evans said he once sent a club an album of photos he took for the game he had been booked for, only to see a player's Instagram account a few hours later with one of his pictures with the watermark removed.

"I wasn't paid and they were just posting them. I am putting all this time and effort in and then that's what you get," he said.

"I have seen people use it for profile pictures and getting rid of the watermark and the quality is bad.

"I pride myself on high-quality photos and to see something that's bad quality, and the photos can be traced back to me. It's not a good look."

After posting about his experience online, Evans said he got an "unbelievable" reaction.

"I have also had local clubs reach out and got bookings since posting. I've also had people who have said they have had similar experiences but to power through."

Evans is also worried about the development of AI and thinks the future is "very scary" for people in his line of work.

"It's only £2 a photo and people are already stealing and, with AI getting better, it may be harder to see the imperfections," he said.

Thorne added that the behaviour pointed to "a much wider problem around AI literacy", adding there was an urgent need for better education about what happens when people upload personal material to AI systems.

Matthew Sammon, a chartered trademark attorney at Sonder & Clay, said copyright belonged to the person who took the photo.

He added that Gilbert was right to say what was going on was theft.

"Photographers use a watermark to protect the image from being copied, if that is removed that is copyright infringement," he said.

He said the owner of the image was entitled to bring legal action, including an injunction to stop any further use of the image, damages for lost income and cover of their legal costs.

But, he added, "one of the difficulties for school photographers is the cost of legal action is expensive".

"In many respects they are reliant on the honesty of their customers, so if they had to launch proceedings they would spend time and effort on that rather than getting on with their job."

articles.title: Deadly crash kills two as plane plunges into 'ball of flames' near suburban golf course
articles.summary: Authorities said a Van's RV-7A crashed near Petaluma Municipal Airport in Northern California, killing two people and sparking a fire that engulfed the aircraft.
articles.body: A small plane crashed shortly after takeoff near a Northern California airport Wednesday morning — killing two people on board and sparking a fire, authorities said. The plane, a Van's RV-7A, crashed shortly after taking off from Petaluma Municipal Airport in Sonoma County, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) told Fox News Digital. The incident took place at around 10:45 a.m. local time on Oct. 7. SKYDIVERS WATCH PLANE VANISH FROM SIGHT, MAKE SPLIT-SECOND DECISION TO JUMP The aircraft went down in a field near Rooster Run Golf Course, where aerial footage showed scattered wreckage and scorched ground, according to FOX 2 San Francisco. Both people on board were killed, Petaluma police told FOX 2. The investigation is being led by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), with the FAA assisting. An NTSB spokesperson told Fox News Digital that a "post-impact fire" erupted after the crash. MIDAIR SCARE FORCES PACKED PASSENGER JET INTO EMERGENCY LANDING, TRAVELERS HOSPITALIZED An investigator was expected to arrive at the scene Thursday to document the wreckage before the aircraft is recovered to a secure facility for further examination. NTSB investigators will review flight tracking data, air traffic control communications, aircraft maintenance records, weather conditions, the pilot's flight experience and witness statements, the official added. Petaluma Police Lt. Zilverio Rivera told reporters the aircraft was "fully engulfed in fire" when emergency crews arrived, FOX 2 reported. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Gary McClintock, who was playing golf nearby at the time of the crash, told FOX 2 he witnessed what appeared to be engine trouble shortly after takeoff. "All of a sudden, the engine kind of stops, sputtering a little bit," McClintock said, as FOX 2 noted. "He starts to dive a little bit." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS He added, "We saw then he makes the turnaround here. It looks like he's trying to make it back to the airport, and you can hear the throttle kick in and, all of a sudden, he just crashed and went down into a ball of flames." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The FAA lists the Van's RV-7A among its eligible amateur-built aircraft kits. The NTSB said a preliminary report is expected within 30 days. A final report identifying the probable cause of the crash could take 12 to 24 months. articles.title: From 19 havai sepoys to a formidable air force in the world, IAF celebrates its 94-year-old glorious journey
articles.summary: HINDON AIR STATION: Indian Air Force, which was established on October 8, 1932, as an auxiliary air force of the British Empire and was then known as the
articles.body: HINDON AIR STATION: Indian Air Force, which was established on October 8, 1932, as an auxiliary air force of the British Empire and was then known as the ‘Royal Indian Air Force’, has since emerged as the world’s third-most powerful air force.As it marked its 94th anniversary at Hindon Air Force Station on Thursday, IAF looked back on its humble beginnings. FIts first operational flight took place on April 1, 1933, with a small but determined group of six RAF-trained officers and 19 Havai Sepoys in four Westland Wapiti IIA biplanes.These formed the nucleus of the ‘A’ Flight at Drigh Road in Karachi and laid the foundation for the planned No. 1 (Army Co-operation) Squadron — marking the dawn of what would evolve into one of the most formidable air forces.Now, armed with a versatile fleet of advanced fighter jets, such as Russian-acquired Sukhois, French Rafale and Mirage, and indigenous Tejas, and transport planes, such as US-acquired Globemaster and Super Hercules, IAF now boasts of 2,353 military aircraft.To mark the day, a piece of IAF’s rich history took to the skies. The vintage Tiger Moth aircraft performed aerobatics before hundreds of spectators, including the three service chiefs, Air Chief Marshal A P Singh, General Dhiraj Seth and Admiral K Swaminathan.IAF pilots Wing Commander Shishir Arora and Grp Capt Amit Dhopawka who flew the Tiger Moth enthralled the audience with their flying skills for around 15 minutes.The vintage aircraft is the sole prized possession of IAF, which is preserved at the station. First built by de Havilland Aircraft Company in the 1930s, originally for the Royal Air Force (RAF) of England, the Tiger Moth fleet served as IAF’s primary basic trainer from 1939 to 1957, with 140 units operated during its active service period. The squadron was phased out in 1957, with one aircraft maintained to remember its past glory.Another key attraction at the event was when outgoing IAF chief ACM Singh arrived at the air base riding a vintage white 1960s Ford Galaxie V8 — a historic American classic car with registration IAF 1 that served as the official staff vehicle for IAF chiefs only on very special occasions.To showcase its air prowess, IAF lined up all its combat aircraft and also showcased its weapons, even those used during Operation Sindoor — like the BrahMoS supersonic cruise missile and the Akash air defence system — which not only stopped Pakistan missile and drone attacks but also razed to ground terrorist hubs and the enemy’s military assets.An all-women IAF’s air warrior drill team ‘Shakti’ memerised spectators with its highly synchronised and complex rifle manoeuvres.IAF drummers’ team, comprising 33 young air warriors dressed in vibrant colours, also captivated the audience with powerful drum beats and dynamic formations.In his last Air Force Day speech, IAF chief ACM Singh, who was given an aerial salute by three Mi-17 1V helicopters carrying the Tricolour and IAF flag, highlighted that “air power is the primary means of protecting the national interest”.He said “an air force can have the most advanced aircraft in the world, but its true strength is measured by its operational preparedness-how quickly and confidently it can act whenever the call comes”.Referring to Operation Sindoor, he pointed out that IAF’s swift transition into combat operations demonstrated its ‘destructive power as well as the effective air defence operations’. He also stressed that “success in modern conflict demands deep synergy” and that joint planning and integrated combat application with Army and Navy is a daily activity.He said, “Space is a natural extension of the air domain”, highlighting the growing collaboration with Isro, especially for the Gaganyaan mission.Congratulating the IAF on its 94th anniversary, PM Narendra Modi posted a video praising the air warriors and said, “India is proud of our Air Warriors. On Air Force Day, we salute their courage and commitment to protect our skies!”Sending his greetings to all the courageous air warriors and their families, defence minister Rajnath Singh in a post on X said, “The Indian Air Force stands as a symbol of courage, valour, discipline and professionalism. With unwavering commitment, our Air Warriors have always guarded the nation’s skies and risen to the occasion whenever the country has faced a crisis. Their dedication and service have not only strengthened India’s security but have also contributed immensely to national unity and the spirit of collective resolve. Salute to our Air Warriors for their courage, commitment and selfless service to the nation.”From securing Indian airspace against hostile intrusions using its fighter jets and delivering precision strikes and air-to-ground attacks to aid Indian Army troops on the battlefield like during the 1971 war and 1999 Kargil war or transporting combat troops, heavy artillery and critical logistics to remote or high-altitude frontiers using its transport workhorses like C-17 Globemaster III, C-130J Super Hercules and An-32 or even gathering real-time intelligence, mapping terrain, and monitoring borders using specialised surveillance and aerial reconnaissance platforms, IAF has served a multi-dimensional role centered on defending national airspace, supporting ground operations, and providing humanitarian assistance.For over nine decades, the IAF and its air warriors have stood the test of time and remained at the forefront of India’s defence, combining courage, discipline and technological excellence in service of the nation.

articles.title: Ontario man with Stage 4 cancer won court battle after OHIP denied US treatment, then province changed the rules; doctors sought funding for US$600,000 TIL therapy in Florida
articles.summary: An Ontario man with Stage 4 melanoma who successfully challenged the province in court over access to potentially life-saving cancer treatment says he is
articles.body: An Ontario man with Stage 4 melanoma who successfully challenged the province in court over access to potentially life-saving cancer treatment says he is now “incredibly disappointed and disheartened” after Ontario changed the rules governing public funding for out-of-country drug treatments.According to CBC News, Alex Shved, 37, took the province to court after the Ontario Health Insurance Plan rejected his oncologist’s request for him to receive tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy, or TIL therapy, in the United States.Shved, a father of two young daughters, has cancer that has spread to his lungs and bones. He has been pursuing every available option in the hope of remaining with his children for as long as possible.His oncologist sought OHIP funding for TIL therapy in Florida, a treatment that would cost approximately US$600,000.Court ruled OHIP had to reconsider his treatment requestOHIP had rejected Shved’s request, citing in part the fact that TIL therapy was under consideration for possible public funding in Ontario.The executive officer of Ontario’s public drug programs argued that routinely paying for out-of-country treatment while a drug is undergoing review could undermine the incentive for manufacturers to participate in Canada’s drug-review and pricing process.Shved challenged the decision in court.In September, the Ontario Divisional Court quashed the OHIP decision and ordered the province to reconsider his application. The court found that OHIP had not provided a sufficient basis for its reasoning, while the judges described the matter as one involving potentially life-or-death consequences for Shved.Following the ruling, however, OHIP rejected Shved’s request for a third time.The development came alongside a change to Ontario’s regulations governing out-of-country drug funding.Shved says government made its previous actions lawfulSpeaking about the province’s response, Shved said the outcome has left him deeply frustrated.“The courts concluded that the government's actions were unlawful, and the government's response was to change the law to make those same actions now lawful,” he said, according to The Canadian Press report.Under the amended rules, Ontario will fund drugs outside the province only when the treatment is already publicly funded in Ontario but access is temporarily unavailable or delayed.Health Minister Sylvia Jones defended the changes, saying the province was protecting Ontario patients and taxpayers from high drug prices while preserving access to treatments that might otherwise be available only in the United States or overseas.The government has also said it is exploring a “mutually satisfactory resolution” in Shved’s individual case. However, Shved said he remains unclear about what that resolution would mean for him.His cancer has spread to his lungs and bonesShved first discovered a growing mole in 2020 and has since undergone multiple treatments.Despite those efforts, his melanoma has progressed and spread to his lungs and bones. His doctors have determined that he could be a suitable candidate for TIL therapy.The treatment is a form of immunotherapy that uses the patient’s own immune cells.Doctors remove tumours from the patient and extract immune cells that have already infiltrated the cancer. Those cells are then multiplied in the laboratory into billions of cells. After chemotherapy prepares the body, the expanded immune cells are infused back into the patient with the aim of attacking the cancer.For Shved, the timing of access is critical.He previously told The Canadian Press that he does not know whether he will remain medically fit, or alive, by the time the treatment is potentially approved for public funding in Ontario.TIL therapy is approved in Canada but not yet publicly funded in OntarioThe dispute comes as TIL therapy moves through Canada’s regulatory and funding systems.A version of the treatment known as lifileucel was approved for sale by Health Canada last year. However, provincial drug plans are still reviewing whether the therapy should be publicly funded.That process can take years.The distinction has become central to Shved’s case. Although the treatment has received regulatory approval in Canada, it is not currently publicly funded in Ontario, meaning patients who need it urgently may face significant barriers to accessing it through the province.Shved’s case has therefore become a broader dispute over what happens when a patient needs an expensive treatment immediately while governments are still negotiating whether and at what price the therapy should be publicly funded.Ontario says the changes protect patients and taxpayersThe Ontario government maintains that its revised regulations are intended to protect the province’s ability to negotiate affordable drug prices and ensure that public funds are used within the established provincial funding system.For Shved, however, the changes have come after he successfully challenged the province’s original decision in court.His legal victory forced OHIP to reconsider his request, but the subsequent regulatory change and third rejection have left him uncertain about whether he will ultimately receive public funding for the treatment he says he urgently needs.As reported, Shved’s court victory has not translated into access to the treatment he was seeking in the United States. Instead, Ontario has moved to clarify and narrow the circumstances in which such out-of-country drug treatment can be publicly funded.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
