articles.title: Pentagon says the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — The firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed, the Pentagon said Thursday, a stunning revelation a...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed, the Pentagon said Thursday, a stunning revelation about plans for the first military execution in more than 65 years after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had described it as being "public."

The Army announced this week that the execution would take place at Fort Hood on Dec. 3 after Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people and injuring 32 others in a shooting at the military base in 2009.

Hegseth, speaking to the conservative TV outlet Real America's Voice on Wednesday, said, "We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public." Officials in the Pentagon clarified Thursday that the execution would be livestreamed and that more details would follow.

The revelation from Hegseth about the public nature of the execution — let alone one as violent as a firing squad — has raised further questions about how the death penalty is carried out in the U.S., especially after the botched lethal injection of Christa Pike in Tennessee.

Experts offer mixed reactions on the plan

Hasan could choose to resist execution and file a habeas petition — a legal request to review the legality of a detention — in civilian court, which could significantly delay the execution, experts said.

"It frankly might outlast the current administration, and who knows if the next one will have the same penchant for executions," said Eugene R. Fidell, a visiting lecturer at Yale Law School specializing in military law.

Deborah Denno, a death penalty expert and law professor at Fordham University, said livestreaming an execution could make the process "much more transparent" and inform the public about all that capital punishment entails. Those are benefits that she said would be useful at a time when Pike's botched execution has raised fresh questions about the manner by which criminal defendants are put to death for their crimes.

"I think it could possibly be a good idea because it would be transparent and the public would be fully aware that it's happening," she said.

When many states have had difficulty carrying out lethal injections due to difficulty accessing drugs or finding medical professionals willing to participate in executions, firing squads are coming to be seen as a less inhumane alternative, said Brenner Fissell, a professor at Villanova Law and vice president of the National Institute of Military Justice.

"Firing squads can be a quicker, cleaner, more precise way to execute a prisoner," he said. "I don't think that's what's motivating this. There's a perceived masculinity and military-ness to firing squads that is part of the aura Hegseth is trying to emphasize — the 'lethality culture.'"

Elisabeth Semel, co-director of the Death Penalty Clinic at UC Berkeley Law, said Hegseth's announcement raises a host of legal and public policy questions, including concerns for the dignity of the defendant, who will be eligible to view the execution and what the Trump administration has in mind in opting for an unusual spectacle.

Though there has been long-running discussion about the idea of televising an execution, "I don't recall a situation in which it was initiated by the government. I think that also raises serious questions about what is the motivation of the government," she said.

"This is a president who's about spectacle and that's, I think, precisely the message that he intends to deliver," Semel said, adding that she was skeptical that the administration had given a second thought to the legal and social questions being presented by the decision.

Trump has spoken out against public executions in Iran

Trump, who approved Hasan's execution, has previously been critical of public executions in Iran, at times using the possibility of protesters being killed by the Iranian government as a possible rationale for military action that preceded his ultimate choice to attack Iran on Feb. 28.

"We've been told that the killing in Iran is stopping," Trump told reporters on Jan. 14. "It's stopping, and there's no plan for executions."

In his State of the Union address just days before launching the Iran war , Trump reiterated, "We stopped them from hanging a lot of them with the threat of serious violence."

The White House on Thursday referred questions about the plans for the livestreamed execution to the Pentagon.

Hegseth was asked Wednesday if Hasan had made any final requests or reached out to the Trump administration. The Pentagon chief replied: "Don't care. We'll see him on Dec. 3."

It's not clear if Hasan will try to appeal

Hasan, an Army psychiatrist who held the rank of major, walked into a medical building on Nov. 5, 2009, where soldiers were waiting in long lines to receive immunizations and medical clearance for deployment. He shouted "Allahu akbar" — Arabic for "God is great!" — and opened fire with a laser-sighted handgun. He also shot at the backs of soldiers fleeing toward the parking lot.

Hasan said it was an effort to stop them from going to Afghanistan and killing his fellow Muslims. A military judge barred him from presenting that as a defense during his 2013 trial. Hasan was left paralyzed from the waist down after being shot in the back by law enforcement, and he now uses a wheelchair.

Hasan could seek a lengthy delay of his execution, though given his behavior at trial, he may not want to.

After firing his lawyers and representing himself, Hasan began his portion of the trial by telling jurors he was the gunman. He said little else over the next three weeks, which convinced his court-appointed standby lawyers that Hasan's only goal was to get a death sentence.

The military called nearly 90 witnesses, but Hasan rested his case without calling a single person to testify in his defense and made no closing argument. Yet he leaked documents during the trial to journalists that revealed him telling military mental health workers that he could " still be a martyr " if executed.

Attorney John Galligan, a former military judge who had represented Hasan in several civil matters following his criminal trial, spoke with Hasan on Wednesday but is barred from offering much detail about that conversation. He is not representing Hasan in his criminal case but said he's worried about his physical health under the plan laid out by officials, and that Hasan has not yet had access to legal counsel.

Galligan said that according to Hasan, the commandant of the facility brought a chaplain but no attorney from either the Trial Defense Service or from his civilian defense when he was notified that Trump had signed off on his execution. Galligan called that a breach of Army regulations.

A spokeswoman for the Army said Thursday that multiple attempts were made to contact Trial Defense Service attorneys, saying they made every reasonable effort and adhered to policy.

"The civilian counsel was not reasonably available to be physically present for the notification on the 5th," the spokeswoman said, adding that counsel was located in Virginia but did not provide a name.

The spokeswoman also said Hasan has not been kept from contacting and communicating with his counsel.

Hegseth said the military hasn't executed a service member by firing squad since World War II. The last military execution took place on April 13, 1961, when Army Pvt. John Bennett was executed by hanging.

Amnesty International said in its report on executions in 2025 that it knew of at least 17 public executions — 11 in Iran and 6 in Afghanistan.

Lauer reported from Philadelphia. Associated Press writers Jonathan J. Cooper in Phoenix, Josh Boak and Michelle L. Price in Washington, and Gene Johnson in Seattle contributed to this report.

articles.title: Haverford professor charged over alleged ‘heinous’ antisemitic online attacks, barred from campus
articles.summary: Haverford College professor Guangtian Ha allegedly sent 50 antisemitic threats to a Jewish colleague using anonymous X accounts, FBI charges reveal.
articles.body: A Haverford College professor was arrested Tuesday and charged with federal cyberstalking after allegedly sending dozens of antisemitic threats to a colleague in Pennsylvania. It prompted the college to bar him from campus, more than two years after Jewish students accused the same professor of making threatening statements about supporters of Israel in a separate lawsuit against the school. Haverford College President Wendy Raymond addressed the arrest of religion professor Guangtian Ha in a statement provided to Fox News Digital by a college spokesperson. "I am heartbroken and furious at the possibility that an individual within our community would seek to inflict such pain on another," Raymond said. "This disturbing news is made even more harmful for many given its proximity to both the Jewish High Holidays and the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks." ISRAELI MEDICS TRAIN US SYNAGOGUES HOW TO RESPOND TO ATTACKS, AS HIGH HOLIDAYS APPROACH According to a federal indictment, Ha allegedly used at least four anonymous X accounts to send approximately 50 threatening messages to a Jewish colleague between October 2025 and May 2026. Prosecutors alleged that Ha posted the colleague's home address, referenced the colleague's children and made statements invoking the Holocaust. The colleague's spouse and three children temporarily left their home twice because of the threats, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer. The arrest follows earlier allegations against Ha that were included in a 2024 antisemitism lawsuit against Haverford College. In a January 2025 amended complaint, Jewish students accused Ha of publishing hostile social media posts about supporters of Israel, including one in which he allegedly said he knew their identities. The complaint reproduced a statement attributed to Ha targeting people within his Haverford community who remained silent about, or supported, what he characterized as genocide. "I will never forgive them," Ha said, according to the complaint. "I know their names and I know their faces. Never forgive. No reconciliation." FBI NABS 7 FOR ALLEGED 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE' TO PRESSURE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN, BUSINESSES OVER ISRAEL TIES The plaintiffs alleged that Ha's remarks were threatening and that college administrators had been informed of his posts by September 2024. They further alleged that Haverford had taken no effective action against him at the time of the January 2025 filing. The earlier lawsuit did not establish that Ha engaged in unlawful conduct, and the allegations in that case are distinct from the federal cyberstalking charge. Raymond said the college had placed Ha, who was already on sabbatical and not teaching during the academic year, on administrative leave pending the criminal proceedings over the "heinous online attacks." "I am deeply distressed by these allegations and want to state in the plainest of terms that any form of harassment or discrimination based on identity is unacceptable, antithetical to our values, and has no place at Haverford," Raymond said. WEAPONIZING THE CHARGE OF GENOCIDE FUELS AN INCREASINGLY DANGEROUS ANTISEMITISM The arrest came just two months after Haverford settled the lawsuit brought by Jewish members of its community over allegations that administrators failed to adequately address antisemitic harassment after Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attacks against Israel. As part of the August settlement, the college committed to annual antisemitism awareness training, revisions to campus policies and the creation of a committee to address antisemitism. A federal judge had previously dismissed the plaintiffs' Title VI discrimination claim while allowing a breach-of-contract claim to proceed. articles.title: Defence secretary talks to German envoy & Greece deputy minister to widen strategic partnerships
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Newly appointed German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck on Thursday met defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh, with the two sides discussing
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Newly appointed German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck on Thursday met defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh, with the two sides discussing India-Germany defence cooperation and the wider strategic partnership. The engagement comes as both countries seek to deepen military and defence-industrial ties, including cooperation in advanced technologies and maritime security.The meeting follows a series of high-level India-Germany defence engagements this year. In April, defence minister Rajnath Singh and German defence minister Boris Pistorius agreed to strengthen co-development and co-production of defence equipment, particularly in niche technologies, while India and Germany also signing a Defence Industrial Cooperation Roadmap aimed at long-term industry-level collaboration.A major element of the expanding partnership is Project-75(I), under which Germany’s Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems and Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders are expected to build six next-generation conventional submarines in India with substantial technology transfer. Wieck said in Sept that the agreement had been finalised on the German side and was awaiting completion of India’s internal processes.Meanwhile, India and Greece also discussed defence and strategic cooperation with a focus on maritime security, coastal security and shipbuilding as the defence secretary met Greece’s deputy minister of Maritime Affairs and Insular Policy Stefanos Gkikas in New Delhi. The engagement highlights the growing maritime dimension of the India-Greece Strategic Partnership.The two sides emphasise their shared interests as major maritime nations, including the need to ensure the safety and security of seafarers.The discussions bring together defence cooperation with the wider maritime domain, covering areas that are important for secure sea lanes, coastal protection and naval capability development. The engagement builds on a broader expansion of India-Greece defence ties.Inaugural session of Indo-Russian working group meetThe inaugural session of the 24th Working Group meeting of the India-Russia intergovernmental commission on Military Technical Cooperation and Defence Industry was held in New Delhi.The session was co-chaired by secretary (defence production) Sanjeev Kumar and first deputy director, FSMTC Andrey A Boytsov, from Russia.Senior officials from both countries joined the deliberations. The discussions were focused on reviewing existing military-technical cooperation and forging co-production and co-development initiatives to further cement the India-Russia strategic partnership in defence.

articles.title: Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad will be livestreamed, Pentagon says
articles.summary: "We'll make sure that people are able to watch it," the US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Thursday.
articles.body:
The public will be able to watch the execution of a former US Army major by firing squad, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has said.

An official from the Defense Department told the BBC the execution of Nidal Hasan, who fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, would be livestreamed.

The Pentagon had announced earlier this week that it would execute Hasan in the first military execution in more than 60 years.

"We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public," Hegseth said on Thursday. "Because people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things."

Hegseth said in an interview with conservative TV outlet Real America's Voice that Hasan is "gonna get a firing squad of soldiers. As it should be".

Asked if Hasan had made any final requests or reached out to President Donald Trump Hegseth said: "Don't care. We'll see him on December 3rd."

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell had said on Monday that the defence secretary had made the recommendation and Trump approved it.

The BBC has contacted the White House for comment on whether Trump supports a livestreamed public execution.

The execution is scheduled to take place at Fort Hood in Texas on 3 December, the secretary of the US Army said on Tuesday. It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two.

Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, admitted in court that he was the gunman in the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

The shooting on 5 November 2009 took place in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.

At court Hasan apologised for "any mistakes". He said during his court martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan.

Fort Hood attacker to be executed by firing squad - a first for US military since World War Two

There is no modern-era precedent for having a public execution, said John Mills, a lawyer who works with inmates sentenced to death.

"It looks to me designed to be a grotesque spectacle," he said. "It's an unprecedented decision in the modern era, and so it is on uncertain legal terrain," he added.

A military execution requires approval from the US president, according to military law. It also requires appellate review, where a higher court inspects the decision, and a final judgment on its legality to move forward.

The appellate process for Hasan is not over, Mills said, and he is likely to seek review of his conviction and sentence in federal court, which would likely stay the execution.

As such, Mills said that he would be surprised if the execution happened.

"Seeking to make it livestreamed, a firing squad execution, is little more than attention-seeking by the Trump administration and is unlikely to occur, much less deliver any semblance of justice," he added.

Certain states require some form of public viewing of executions. Many states require journalists to be present, and the person due to be executed can invite people. Others also allow ordinary citizens to volunteer as witnesses.

But "there hasn't ever been a livestreamed execution," says Deborah Denno, a law professor at Fordham University, who has studied US execution methods.

A livestreamed execution would "force a level of transparency that we have probably never seen before in this country", she says.

"More than half of the country wants the death penalty - even though that's on the decline - an argument could be made that 'if you want the death penalty, then we are going to show you how it's conducted in this country'. And people would have to realise exactly what's happening in a way that many people ignore."

Denno says there are important considerations for a livestream such as whether it would be age-redistricted and whether it would contravene the policies of the online platform that hosts the viewing.

It is unclear where the livestream will be available. Most major social media platforms have rules that prohibit or restrict livestreaming explicit content.

I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's

While there were more than 2,700 executions across 17 countries last year, only two countries carried them out publicly.

Eleven public executions were known to have been carried out in Iran in 2025, and another six in Afghanistan, according to Amnesty International.

The countries with the highest number of executions last year were China, Iran, Saudi Arabia, Yemen and the US, in that order, Amnesty International data shows.

While Trump has never publicly advocated for a public execution, he has long supported the death penalty. In 1989, for example, he took out large ads in The New York Times calling for the execution of the Central Park Five - who had been convicted of rape and assault charges but were later exonerated.

Trump has previously condemned public executions in Iran, and has cited the Iranian government's potential killing of protesters as a possible justification for military intervention before attacking the country earlier this year.

The US government had not executed anyone for 17 years until the final year of Trump's first term as president, when the government conducted a flurry of 13 executions.

Upon returning to office last January, Trump swiftly overturned predecessor Joe Biden's moratorium on federal executions and signed an executive order aimed at "restoring" the death penalty and "protecting public safety".

The last military execution in the country took place in 1961, when a US Army private was hanged after being convicted of raping an 11-year-old Austrian girl. The execution was authorised by then-President Dwight D Eisenhower and took place despite the victim's family asking his successor, John F Kennedy, for clemency.

The last military execution by firing squad took place in January 1945, when a young US Army deserter, Eddie Slovik, was shot during the final months of the World War Two.

articles.title: Trump awards Musk and other tech titans National Medals of Science
articles.summary: President Donald Trump joined Michael Kratsios to award the Medal of Science to Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su and Sergey Brin amid announcements about new science funding.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump joined some of America’s most powerful tech leaders Thursday at a summit the White House billed as the start of a “golden age” of American science. Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, AMD CEO Lisa Su, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and Dell founder Michael Dell gathered with Trump and a host of administration officials and scientific luminaries for the Science: A New Golden Age Summit at the U.S. Institute of Peace. “We live in an age of American wonders and technological marvels, and with the help of the brilliant men and women here today, we will always be on top,” Trump said. Trump awarded the National Medal of Science to Musk, Brin, Huang and Su. He awarded the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Nadella and Dell. Trump presented each of the recipients with medals and certificates of honor, later asking some of their families to join him onstage to take photos. “You’re going to go down in the annals of history as being great,” Trump told the recipients. White House spokesperson Liz Huston said in a statement: “The Trump Administration is grateful for the contributions of these incredible leaders in science and technology. These recipients are helping ensure America keeps leading the world in innovation.” The celebration took place just hours after Vice President JD Vance announced that the Trump administration would suspend Microsoft, whose CEO was a guest of honor at the event, and several other companies from a program that allows foreign workers to apply for green cards. Several of the summit’s speakers emphasized the importance of immigrants to America’s scientific power. “I was an immigrant, and my parents brought us here to pursue the American dream,” Huang told NBC News as he walked through the venue with his parents. “It’s an incredible honor and something that could only happen here in America.” Carnegie Mellon University President Farnam Jahanian highlighted the importance of a welcoming immigration system in a conversation about the future of American research universities. Jahanian pointed out that China produces more engineers and scientists than the U.S., Europe and Japan put together. “We need to have an immigration policy that can recruit the best talent to come to this country, speaking as an immigrant who has benefited from the opportunities this country has,” Jahanian said. “It’s important to recruit the best talent to come here so they stay here and contribute.” The summit, an all-day affair meant to highlight the American scientific enterprise, built on a July report from Michael Kratsios, head of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, about how the Trump administration aims to reinvigorate scientific discovery and innovation. “This is the golden age,” Trump said, taking the stage to kick off the celebration’s afternoon program. “We are an extremely high-IQ audience for a change,” he said, drawing chuckles from the audience. The Science: A New Golden Age report and Thursday’s gathering aim to tackle what the White House sees as growing scientific bureaucracy and stagnating innovation. Kratsios highlighted the ballooning costs of clinical trials and the falling rates of novel drugs approved for patient use as examples of increased scientific sluggishness. The report says the administration will streamline funding to promising scientists instead of routing it through established institutions. The event kicked off with a series of announcements about funding for new scientific initiatives. Among them is a pledge of around $2.4 billion of AI computing credits and scientific tools by America’s leading AI companies for federal agencies working on a variety of scientific issues prioritized by the White House. The areas include quantum algorithms, AI-driven physical laboratories and improvement of the efficiency of nuclear engineering. Kratsios also presided over an announcement by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and Energy Secretary Chris Wright of a new partnership to embrace nuclear technology in space exploration. “Thanks to President Trump, America’s nuclear renaissance is reaching a new frontier,” Wright said. Isaacman said nuclear power would allow NASA spacecraft to travel farther and operate longer, “opening an entirely new frontier for exploration and discovery.” The day focused on a handful of scientific fields, including artificial intelligence — now referred to as “super intelligence” by the Trump administration — nuclear power, quantum computing and metascience, or the study of science itself. “Super intelligence is going to be the biggest unlock for scientists,” Kratsios said, opening the celebration. Representatives from America’s leading AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Amazon Web Services and Micron Technology, took the stage to announce their new partnerships with the federal government. A variety of scientists from academic institutions and companies gave a series of lightning talks about their research, which largely focused on nuclear energy and using AI to accelerate their research. The speakers oscillated between using “AI” and “SI” — the term preferred by administration officials since Trump issued an executive order renaming the technology. John Martinis, a professor of physics at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and recipient of the Nobel Prize in physics, said the technology was already accelerating his group’s research. Asked what a golden age of science would look like to him, Martinis said he didn’t have to look far. “I feel like we’re in it right now,” he said. “It’s really exciting what’s happening with SI.”

articles.title: USS Lincoln docks in San Diego Bay following scrutinized 322-day deployment
articles.summary: Families of crewmembers arrived hours ahead of the carrier’s return after reported suicide attempts, dwindling supplies and harsh conditions became synonymous with its deployment.
articles.body: ABOARD THE USS ABRAHAM LINCOLN — Draped in red, white and blue striped banners, the USS Abraham Lincoln arrived in San Diego Bay after 322 days at sea. It ended one of the longest maritime deployments in U.S. military history, returning home to eager loved ones, as well as ongoing scrutiny over past reports of low morale. Elated crew members lined the decks portside — some waved to the waiting crowds, and others danced as their loved ones cheered from below. “It’s a combination of the day before Christmas and the last day of school,” the commanding officer, Capt. Dan Keeler, told NBC News, adding that some of the crewmembers are just 18 years old. “They are amazing, you know, legends and heroes,” he said. “Every single one of them.” Among the first to depart from Naval Air Station North Island in Coronado will be 64 parents who have been waiting months to meet their babies for the first time, The Associated Press reported. Sailor Brent Ledbetter told NBC News that he has watched his son grow via videos and photos sent from his wife, an air traffic control officer who was also assigned to the ship. She was relieved of duty because of her pregnancy. “I just want to hold him, play with him,” Ledbetter said. The Lincoln’s return to Coronado caps off more than 10 months of U.S. military engagement in the Middle East. The aircraft carrier drew national attention over reports of supply shortages and at least eight suicide attempts. The ship was deployed as a part of Operation Epic Fury, a mission that was “laser-focused” on destroying Iranian offensive missiles and missile production, Iran’s navy and other security infrastructure, the Defense Department said in February. It was at sea without a port call for 286 days, the second-longest deployment since the Vietnam War, and surpassed 300 consecutive days overseas overall. The USS Gerald R. Ford set the record for longest deployment by an aircraft carrier at 326 days, which ended this year, the AP reported. Families and loved ones of crewmembers arrived hours ahead of the carrier’s return Thursday, waiting in line to get on the naval base near San Diego. The Lincoln and its air wing dropped more than 1,145 weapons in its 10 months at sea. Some of the crew painted a mural depicting the 1,463 objects hit during Operation Epic Fury. “Over on the far right, you can see all the submarines that were sunk by the strike group, and then down below, we’re still working on it, but that’s going to represent every bomb that was dropped on an air surface target,” said Cmdr. Cody Forsythe, an air operations officer who is among the 5,000 crewmembers aboard the aircraft carrier. A mural like this is rare in the armed services, he said. Forsythe estimates the last time service members undertook a project similar to the mural was back in the 1940s. Crewmember Isabella Norfleet said, “We try to make our impact on the boat, make it last, make the morale better.” Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth flew out to the carrier Wednesday to give the crew the Presidential Unit Citation, the highest honor a unit can receive, which is typically reserved for significant achievement in combat. He pushed back against what he said were efforts to turn the “Lincoln into some sort of a symbol, a symbol of dysfunction or a symbol of low morale or a symbol of a failed mission.” “I draw inspiration from the mission that you executed so successfully. You have changed the arc of history,” he said.

images.caption: Sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln Nimitz-class aircraft carrier wave to friends and family members as the ship docks at its homeport at Naval Air Station North Island on return from a historic 10-month deployment on Oct. 8, 2026, in Coronado, Calif. The USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72) set a U.S. Navy record spending over 260 days consecutively at sea without a port call while playing a key role in Operation Epic Fury and regional maritime security operations in the Middle East.

articles.title: ICE agents involved in Bronx shooting that leaves 1 person injured: NYPD
articles.summary: A shooting involving federal law enforcement agents in the Marble Hill neighborhood of the Bronx left one person hospitalized Thursday afternoon, according to the NYPD
articles.body: A person was shot during an incident involving U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents in the Bronx on Thursday afternoon, according to information provided to Fox News Digital. The shooting occurred around 4 p.m. in the Marble Hill neighborhood of the Bronx, the New York Police Department (NYPD) said in a post on X. The person who was shot was taken to a nearby hospital, where they were conscious and receiving medical attention, according to the NYPD. The person's identity and the extent of their injuries were not immediately known. MAMDANI DINED AT NYC RESTAURANT LINKED TO ANTI-ISRAEL MENU AFTER BEING BOOED AT OCT 7 VIGIL: REPORT NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani took to X to denounce the shooting, stating that he contacted President Donald Trump over the incident. Mamdani wrote that agents allegedly surrounded a man and a child who were inside a vehicle before firing. He said the child was believed to be unharmed. Federal authorities have not publicly confirmed those details. "This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation," Mamdani wrote. "I have called the President; when we speak I will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city." The mayor also called for ICE to be abolished and demanded that federal immigration agents leave city neighborhoods, hospitals and streets.MOM DIES SHIELDING BABY IN HORRIFIC 15-STORY BRONX FALL AS POLICE HUNT SUSPECT: REPORT The NYPD said its officers were not involved in the shooting and were not at the scene when it occurred. An NYPD spokesperson told Fox News Digital that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is investigating the incident and directed additional questions to federal authorities.New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said Thursday that she had been briefed on the shooting and called on federal authorities to provide a full account of what happened. "We expect federal authorities to provide a full and transparent accounting of the circumstances surrounding this incident," Hochul wrote in a post on X. "New Yorkers deserve to know exactly what happened and why." articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid a rapid absorption of mobile phones and technology PM Narendra Modi called for a global effort to tackle cyber frauds and deepfakes, while asserting that phones were no longer communication devices but a powerful tool of governance.Addressing the India Mobile Congress, the PM said his govt had leveraged technology and connectivity for direct benefit transfer of Rs 50 lakh crore, which helped plug leakages of nearly Rs 5 lakh crore. "Those whose easy earnings have stopped, will they love Modi? ...They may shout and scream as much as they want, but I will continue in this direction," he said at a time when opposition has mounted pressure over SIR.Recalling launch of 5G from the same platform in 2022, he sought to contrast the situation over a decade back when "digital divide was a challenge (and) new tech was becoming a privilege". Now, the "telecom revolution", he said, is driving service delivery, content, including in local languages, and gaming, but it came with challenges."At a time when telecom and digital technology are playing such a critical role, it is equally important that we strengthen the security framework associated with them," PM said, while urging govts, technology companies, telecom operators, and financial institutions to work together."I urge GSMA and telecom operators to come together and create a global mechanism to stop frauds even before they reach people. India has learned a great deal through its own experiences, and is ready to share the same with the world."Modi said the telecom boom was driven by a well-crafted policy framework, which sought to untangle the sector and also reduce AGR and other liabilities.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Proof of 21 'compromised transfers', 11 policy changes part of CBI's Punjab file
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A day before the Supreme Court is scheduled to take up a plea for restraining its probe into allegations against OSD to Punjab CM Bhagwant
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A day before the Supreme Court is scheduled to take up a plea for restraining its probe into allegations against OSD to Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann, CBI was learnt to be in possession of evidence of "compromised transfers" of at least 21 senior state govt and police officers of Punjab.The evidence, collected as part of its probe into the "cash-for-postings" scam, includes an alleged push for the transfer of a senior cop from the anti-gangster task force and the suspension of an officer of Sangrur jail. CBI, based on ED probe, has mentioned alleged instances of Mann's OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman's role in its FIR against him.Eleven alleged instances of changes in policy, including bid to influence the transport policy and administrative decisions, have also been cited. articles.title: UK engineers started with previously unwanted steel instead of a bridge design; they built the Tan House Footbridge around the available material to cut embodied carbon
articles.summary: A new footbridge in Wokingham, UK, was designed around steel that had already been used or was previously considered unwanted.
articles.body: A new footbridge in Wokingham, UK, was designed around steel that had already been used or was previously considered unwanted. The approach allowed engineers to rethink the bridge design based on the material that was already available. According to the research published in The Structural Engineer, titled ‘Tan House Footbridge: Designing with repurposed steel, from early design stages to fabrication’, the bridge was designed, detailed and fabricated between February 2022 and October 2024. The team used digital design methods to test different options while tracking material use and embodied carbon savings throughout the design process. The project was delivered through a collaboration between Network Rail, WSP UK and Format Engineers.How repurposed steel shaped the Tan House Footbridge designRepurposed steel was central to the design of Tan House Footbridge. The team used creative digital techniques to adapt the bridge’s structural form to the available stock of previously unwanted steel. This allowed the material itself to influence the design from an early stage rather than being selected after the structure had been developed.Generative digital methods gave the team a flexible, iterative design process. Engineers could test different options, adjust the structure to suit available materials, and track potential savings in material use and embodied carbon at each stage leading to fabrication. This approach helped connect early design decisions with carbon reduction.Digital methods helped refine the bridge around repurposed steelThe engineers used generative digital methods to keep the design process flexible and test different options. These tools allowed the team to compare designs while tracking changes in material use and embodied carbon as the bridge developed.The design could then be reviewed and adjusted at each stage towards fabrication. Instead of settling on one design at the outset, the team could assess different possibilities and refine the structure as the available repurposed steel became clearer.This flexibility was important because the existing steel directly influenced the bridge’s structural form. Digital tools helped engineers match the design to the available material while continuing to assess the material and embodied carbon savings associated with each option.Tan House Footbridge combined bespoke design with lower embodied carbonTan House Footbridge was designed, detailed and fabricated between February 2022 and October 2024. The project focused on using repurposed or reclaimed material while still delivering a bespoke bridge suited to its site.The design process continued from the early stages through to fabrication. This allowed the team to assess material choices and their effects throughout the development of the bridge.The research states that the team believed Tan House had the lowest embodied carbon of any footbridge Network Rail had constructed on a live site at the time of writing.An internal Network Rail and design team study also found that Tan House had considerably lower CO₂ emissions than Network Rail's standard Series 400 steel rail bridge.How did the Tan House project reduce embodied carbonThe Tan House project also challenged the idea that a bespoke bridge must require higher capital expenditure or greater embodied carbon. The team found that a site-specific design could work with repurposed material while keeping carbon emissions lower.The project shows how the choice of materials can influence a structure before construction begins. By considering existing steel during the design process, the engineers were able to develop the bridge around material that was already available.The digital workflow also allowed the team to compare options and follow material and embodied carbon savings through fabrication. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Evidence cited by World Bank suggests that unrestricted use of generative AI can improve what students submit as part of classwork while weakening what they actually learn - a warning with implications for countries such as India.World Development Report 2026 devotes a section to 'Generative AI and the Erosion of Knowledge, Learning, and Human Skills', cautioning that tools such as ChatGPT can reduce the mental effort through which reasoning, writing and knowledge are built.Its strongest evidence comes from China. A study covering students in classes VII-XII found self-reported AI use rising from almost zero to around 80% between 2022 and 2025. Six months after its first use, homework scores improved 18% even as students spe-nt less time on assignments, while monthly in-class examination scores fell 20%. Students who had ever used AI also scored, on average, 5-7% lower in senior high-school and college entrance exams.The report cautioned that the study had not yet been peer-reviewed and reflected the early phase of AI adoption.Gaurav Nayyar, who led the World Bank team that prepared the report, said the evidence points to both opportunity and risk in education. "If students outsource the learning process to AI, then... that will be a problem," he told TOI.He said the evidence so far appeared more encouraging when AI was used by teachers rather than directly by students, pointing to its use in personalising and customising instructions to suit different learners.Other research reviewed by World Bank points in the same direction. Participants using large language models for research displayed lower cognitive effort and weaker reasoning, while studies found mental effort declining even when output quality improved. Students given unrestricted AI access also performed worse later when the technology was withdrawn.The report warns that if students use AI to complete homework, the "productive struggle" central to learning can disappear, potentially weakening foundational skills in reasoning and writing.But it does not argue against AI in education. A synthesis of experiments across China, Ghana, Nigeria, Turkiye and US found that 30 sessions of AI-powered tutoring produced learning gains equivalent to at least 0.5 years of schooling, particularly when AI complemented teachers and included safeguards against shortcuts. "AI can augment human capabilities," the report said, "but it must not replace the processes through which more advanced skills are acquired."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Israel kills or wounds Palestinian every 90 minutes in Gaza since ceasefire
articles.summary: Islamic Relief calls for global action as deadly Israeli attacks in Gaza continue and humanitarian conditions worsen.
articles.body:
Israeli attacks have killed or wounded a Palestinian in Gaza every 90 minutes on average since the ceasefire was announced in October last year, the aid group Islamic Relief says.

Islamic Relief, a United Kingdom-based charity, said on Thursday that at least 1,454 Palestinians were killed and more than 5,000 wounded over the year. At least 320 of those killed were children, close to one a day.

Gaza’s Health Ministry reported that 1,471 Palestinians have been killed and 5,189 wounded since the ceasefire, including four killed and 28 wounded in the past 24 hours.

Israel has killed at least 74,254 people since October 2023, the ministry added.

On Thursday, Israeli forces killed a Palestinian southeast of Deir el-Balah, in central Gaza, and an Israeli air strike on a house in central Khan Younis wounded several people, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

In the occupied West Bank, a 13-year-old boy was shot in the foot during an Israeli raid on Yamoun, west of Jenin, the Palestinian Red Crescent said.

Islamic Relief said Israel has used the so-called Yellow Line , which marks the area under Israeli military control, to push Palestinians out of 65 percent of Gaza, crowding its nearly 2.1 million people into the remaining 35 percent.

According to the report, an Islamic Relief aid worker in Gaza whose name is withheld for their safety said: “There is no ceasefire in reality. They target displacement camps and crowded areas, so there is still a lot of fear.”

Israel continues to block shelter materials, fuel and medical supplies, the group said.

About 82 percent of Gaza’s structures are damaged or destroyed, more than half of health services have shut down and more than 20,000 severely ill patients are denied permission to leave for treatment.

The charity urged world leaders to increase pressure to protect civilians and uphold international law.

“A ceasefire in name only cannot be an excuse for international inaction,” it said.

articles.title: Lansing police chief warns there may be a serial killer in Michigan’s capital city
articles.summary: Five people have died along a river trail in Lansing since last October. Authorities are investigating whether the deaths are connected.
articles.body: A series of deaths along a short stretch of a river trail in Michigan’s capital city may be the result of a serial killer, authorities said. The five deaths span nearly a year, beginning last October, and all of them appear to involve victims who were homeless, Lansing Police Chief Robert Backus told reporters last week. “One question that we are being asked is ‘Do we have a serial killer in Lansing?’” Backus said. “What we need the public to know is that we are investigating all of these cases. They are all active investigations, and we are looking at the idea or the possibility that these may be related cases.” Three of the deaths were determined to be homicides, Backus said. The manner of death for the remaining two is unclear. One was ruled undetermined, Backus said, and a finding has not yet been issued in the other death. A suspect was arrested in connection with one of the homicides — the Aug. 20 stabbing of Daniel Lusk, 22, Backus said. That suspect, Edward Smith, 24, has not been charged in any of the other deaths. His attorney did not immediately respond to a request for comment Thursday. The four other deaths involve what Backus described as blunt force traumatic injuries to the face. No weapon has been identified. Those victims are Gino Chouinard, 54, who died Oct. 14, 2025; Denis Dunnebacke, 70, who was found unresponsive on July 9 and died three days later; Robert Smith, 57, who was found unresponsive on July 13 and died four days later; and Louis Woodruff, 57, who was hospitalized Aug. 30 and died Sept. 1. The men were found along a roughly 1.5-mile section of trail near downtown Lansing, according to locations provided by the police department. “When I’m reporting these patterns to you, I wish I had more information to share,” Backus said. “I wish I could be more certain and concrete in what I say, but there are challenges in these cases.” Among those challenges, Backus said, are the locations and times of the events that led to the deaths. There are no cameras or witnesses, he said, and the assaults are believed to have taken place in the early morning. The police department set up camera trailers along the trail, he said, and night shift officers have been assigned to patrol the area. Asked at a news conference whether the police department should have warned the public after Dunnebacke’s death in July — he was the second man to die — Backus said it wasn’t immediately clear that his injuries were the result of an assault. Hospital staff members initially believed his death could have been from a medical issue, Backus said, though it was investigated by police major crimes investigators and treated as a “suspicious situation.” The manner of Dunnebacke’s death has not yet been determined, Backus said.

articles.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire breaks silence to BBC
articles.summary: Vitalii Zhykovych gives his own account of the attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev.
articles.body:
A former Ukrainian security services officer linked to a bomb attack in Monaco in June that targeted a multi-millionaire says he believed it was ordered by senior members of HUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency.

In an exclusive interview with the BBC from prison in Kyiv, facilitated by his lawyer, Vitalii Zhykovych has given his own account of the attempted assassination for the first time.

Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev and his 13-year-old son were badly hurt in the blast and his partner suffered catastrophic injuries. Yermolayev later described their survival as "nothing short of a miracle".

Zhykovych describes himself as a "freelancer" for Ukraine's SBU security service and says Anastasia Berezovska, the woman caught on camera planting the bomb in Monaco, was his "agent".

A week after the bombing, Berezovska's body was discovered in the woods west of Kyiv with gunshot wounds to the head.

But Zhykovych insists he did not send her to kill, and nor did he kill her.

He was arrested and accused of her murder together with an active-duty intelligence officer from HUR called Vladyslav Reut.

Reut initially confessed to investigators, and led them to the shallow grave. But days later in court, he changed his testimony to blame Zhykovych.

Ukrainian agent accused of murdering Monaco bomb suspect changes story

For a long time, Zhykovych himself stayed silent.

Now, responding to questions from the BBC, he alleges that Reut - who he refers to as "The Boss" - had "proposed the operation" in Monaco against Vadym Yermolayev.

He understood it was an official mission.

"As Reut informed me, this operation […] had been authorised and approved by Reut's superiors, who served in the Main Intelligence Directorate of the Ministry of Defence [HUR]," he says.

Distancing himself from the explosion itself, he alleges that Reut asked to use Berezovska for the bombing and when Zhykovych refused – he says she was not fully trained – Reut agreed to send her for reconnaissance instead.

Reut then communicated directly with Bereszovska without including him, according to Zhykovych, who alleges that Reut also provided her with the explosives.

The BBC asked HUR to comment on the latest claims. The agency has previously said that it is "committed to a full investigation" and providing "comprehensive support" to law enforcement bodies.

The SBU has described Zhykovych in a statement only as a "former law enforcement officer".

Yermolayev was attacked in Monaco as he and his family were returning from an evening meal on the seafront. A surveillance video shows Berezovska walking slightly in front of the group, then leaving the device in a bag on their doorstep.

It detonates just as they get close, apparently shocking even Berezovska with its force.

Yermolayev later said he believed that serving HUR officers, "individuals close to the agency's current and former leadership", were linked to the attack.

He called for "the truth, protection, and justice".

Berezovska was quickly identified as the suspected bomber and on 2 July her image, taken from CCTV footage, was circulated by Interpol.

She had already fled, first driving through Italy and Germany, then taking a bus from Frankfurt to Ukraine.

Before she could be caught and questioned though, she was driven to the woods by Reut and Zhykovych and killed. Each blames the other for her shooting.

The shocking case has prompted intense speculation, including over who may have wanted Yermolayev dead and why, and whether this could have been a state-ordered assassination attempt, a rogue operation or some kind of criminal score-settling.

The businessman himself, who renounced his Ukrainian passport some years ago and now has Cypriot citizenship, has dismissed multiple theories.

They include the idea the attack might be linked to a struggle between organised crime groups involved in highly lucrative scam call-centres in Ukraine.

Earlier this year, a court in Estonia convicted Yermolayev's son, Artur, of defrauding its citizens out of millions of euros through such "offisy", as the scam networks are known in Ukraine.

Vadym Yermolayev told the Ukrainska Pravda newspaper that he "never had anything to do with anything" in the case.

Now Zhykovych has put forward his own theory to us.

He alleges that Reut told him the bombing was in retaliation for "funding the annexation of Crimea", which he understood to mean Yermolayev was paying taxes to Russia from businesses in Russian-occupied Crimea.

"In my view, this constitutes grounds for the operation," he communicated from prison.

Yermolayev has repeatedly denied any remaining business interests linked to Russia.

At his most recent custody hearing in Kyiv, surrounded by heavily armed guards, Zhykovych spoke publicly for the first time since his arrest. The BBC were the only media present.

At one point Zhykovych said Reut had in fact told him the attack in Monaco was not "authorised".

"Someone had ordered this target from the civilian side," Zhykovych said, without explaining.

The judge then interrupted, reminding him that he was addressing an open court.

Zhykovych also revealed that Reut originally talked of two targets.

When we asked, he said he could not disclose the second name. Other sources strongly suggest it was a pro-Russian blogger tried and convicted in absentia last year by Ukraine of treason.

As the investigation continues – into both the bombing in Monaco and the murder in Ukraine - Berezovska's family have many questions of their own.

The 39-year-old had been in Germany since early 2022, when she left Ukraine as a refugee with her young son.

Zhykovych now claims she was living a double-life, working with him as an agent "against Muscovy" – meaning Russia.

He said they had met online and told us the pair were working to "repel the armed aggression of the Russian Federation".

Berezovska's husband has told the BBC that the allegation was "nonsense". He believes she was dragged, unwittingly, into the whole affair.

Zhykovych says Berezovska called him the day after the Monaco attack, and when he asked why she had done it, she said Reut had promised her a huge fee. "$50,000 doesn't just lie on the streets," she supposedly explained.

Residents in her village have told us that Berezovska was saving to buy a flat. But when she travelled to Ukraine to collect the money, she was lured into the woods and shot.

Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko and Volodymyr Lozhko.

articles.title: France turned 127 hectares of abandoned gravel pits into Europe’s largest floating solar farm; 135,000 panels now generate power for 37,000 people
articles.summary: France has turned a former gravel-quarry site in Haute-Marne into Europe’s largest floating solar farm, covering 127 hectares and carrying 135,000
articles.body: France has turned a former gravel-quarry site in Haute-Marne into Europe’s largest floating solar farm, covering 127 hectares and carrying 135,000 photovoltaic modules. The Les Ilots Blandin project near Perthes began operating in June 2025, using quarry basins to produce renewable electricity. With a total capacity of 74.3 MW, the installation is expected to generate power for around 37,000 people annually while avoiding massive CO2 emissions. Q ENERGY and Grand Est Development International provided these details about the project.How did France turn 127 hectares of gravel pits into Europe’s largest floating solar farmThe project was built on 6 unused basins created by former gravel extraction at the Blandin site. According to Grand Est Developpement International, the 127-hectare site had been left after quarrying activity and was repurposed rather than using a new area of land for the solar installation. The organisation describes the project as Europe’s largest floating solar park.Q ENERGY began developing the project in 2019, with the idea of using unused industrial basins for renewable energy. The company said the former gravel pits were suitable because they offered strong solar potential while creating little conflict over land use. The quarry operations were due to end in 2020.The location also meant the project could make use of water surfaces that had already been created by industrial activity. Instead of covering open ground with solar panels, much of the installation sits on floating structures placed across the former quarry basins.What makes the Les Ilots Blandin project so largeThe scale becomes clearer from the number of panels involved. More than 135,000 photovoltaic modules have been installed across the site on floating platforms developed in France. Grand Est Developpement International says the project involved about 100 people, while construction took 15 months.The solar panels themselves cover 45.5 hectares, even though the overall project extends across 127 hectares. Balkan Green Energy News reports that 72.3 MW of the plant’s capacity is installed on floating platforms, while another 2 MW comes from a ground-mounted section. The 6 floating platforms range from 8 MW to 17 MW each.That small ground-mounted section was included for practical reasons. Q ENERGY says the 2 MW system was designed into the project to improve the overall energy output and economic performance of the site.Electricity production capacity of the floating solar farmThe plant has a total capacity of 74.3 MWp. Q ENERGY says it can generate enough renewable electricity each year to supply 37,000 people and is expected to prevent 18,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions annually.The electricity output gives the former industrial site a new role. What was once associated with gravel extraction is now being used to produce power without requiring the entire project to occupy additional land.The installation was officially inaugurated on 20 June 2025. Q ENERGY said construction began in September 2023 after more than five years of planning, with the plant reaching full commissioning in June 2025.Why was floating solar chosen for the former quarriesFloating solar is still an emerging technology in France, particularly in the northern parts of the country. Q ENERGY says such projects can make use of areas where land-use conflicts are limited, but they also face a significant financial challenge.Floating installations generally cost more to construct and maintain than conventional ground-mounted solar farms. Balkan Green Energy News reports that they must also compete directly with ground-based solar projects in France’s public tender system rather than having a separate tender process.That made the design and economics of Les Ilots Blandin especially important. Q ENERGY said several configurations were considered before the final arrangement was selected, including the addition of the 2 MW ground-mounted section.Companies involved in bringing the project into operationLes Ilots Blandin was developed through a partnership involving several companies. Q ENERGY initiated the project, while Ciel & Terre supplied and installed the floating structures, solar modules and inverters. Perpetum handled the electrical infrastructure and construction of the ground-mounted array, while Solutions30 was responsible for cabling, grid connection and overall commissioning.Funding for construction was secured in September 2024, with more than €50 million raised through Credit Agricole Transitions & Energies and Bpifrance. In early 2025, Spanish renewable energy company Velto Renewables acquired a 50% stake and became the long-term owner of the asset.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pennsylvania school district unveils plans for gender-neutral ‘universal toilet rooms’
articles.summary: Strath Haven High School's $76 million renovation includes "universal toilet rooms" on every floor, with cameras and walled-off stalls to curb loitering.
articles.body: A Pennsylvania high school is planning to build gender-neutral bathroom facilities as part of a massive renovation project estimated to cost approximately $76 million, according to architectural plans presented to the local school board. The Wallingford-Swarthmore School District's Sept. 15 schematic design presentation for Strath Haven High School includes plans for "universal toilet rooms" on multiple floors of the building, along with a rendering showing individual bathroom stalls and a shared sink area. The proposed bathroom overhaul is part of a broader renovation that includes new science classrooms, infrastructure improvements and expanded academic space. The district's own student newspaper, The Panther Press, reported that the project would replace existing gendered bathrooms with larger universal facilities on each floor. WEST VIRGINIA PRINCIPAL SUSPENDED AFTER RECORDING DEVICES FOUND IN GIRLS’ LOCKER ROOMS Architectural plans presented to the Wallingford-Swarthmore School District in September show proposed "universal toilet rooms" on all four floors of Strath Haven High School as part of a $76 million renovation proposal. "The plan also includes a complete reconstruction of the building’s bathrooms," the Panther Press reported Sept. 29. "In place of the current gendered bathrooms, the plan proposes to create a new and larger universal gender-neutral bathroom on each floor. The model also includes a separate faculty toilet only accessible from the hallway." The student newspaper reported that the architect for the plan, Mike Kelly of Kelly Clough Baker and Associates, said that the new bathrooms would allow cameras inside while the stalls are designed to be completely walled off and hidden from the cameras. The outlet reported that Kelly said this would assist the administration’s control of the bathrooms and address loitering in the bathroom. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION OPENS FOUR TITLE IX INVESTIGATIONS INTO MICHIGAN AND NORTH CAROLINA SCHOOL DISTRICTS "We’ve seen this in a lot of schools really cutting down on behavior issues that happen in restrooms," Kelly said. The Wallingford-Swarthmore School District confirmed to Fox News Digital that "the district has developed plans to create universal toilet rooms for students." "As has been the case in a growing number of middle and high schools, this design was selected to enhance student privacy, safety and supervision," the spokesperson said. "Each student will have access to an acoustically separated, fully enclosed private toilet room, providing a level of privacy that exceeds what is available in a traditional school restroom configuration. The Wallingford-Swarthmore Board of School Directors recently approved the schematic design as part of the Strath Haven High School renovation project. DAD OF THIRD-GRADE GIRL IN MASSACHUSETTS ALLEGEDLY BARGED IN ON BY TRANS STUDENT IN BATHROOM CALLS FOR ACTION "Each toilet room will be fully enclosed with floor-to-ceiling walls and doors and will be acoustically separated from adjacent rooms. In addition, each room will be equipped with vape detection technology and fire alarm devices. Cameras will monitor entry and exit areas outside the bathrooms, providing enhanced supervision while maintaining privacy within the individual rooms." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The spokesperson added that some traditional restroom layouts in the existing school will remain, and the Board of School Directors approved a project budget capped at $70 million, with most of the funding dedicated to upgrading and renovating the existing school’s infrastructure. The district said additional details on costs and budget allocations are available in its publicly posted schematic design presentation.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill denies most abuse claims but admits to shoving wife into wall in explosive testimony
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill admitted to pushing Lakeeta Vaccaro Hill into a wall and threatening her but denied multiple other battery allegations on the witness stand.
articles.body: Free agent NFL wide receiver Tyreek Hill took the witness stand in his divorce and battery civil case in Miami on Thursday, and it was as explosive as his speed and play-making ability on the field. During approximately two hours of testimony, Hill ... …Claimed his 18-month marriage to Lakeeta Vaccaro Hill was punctuated by arguments about her refusal to sign a post-nuptial agreement, her stealing between $60,000-$100,000 a month from a family account, her insistence his family leave their sprawling Broward County estate, and occasionally him flirting with other women. TYREEK HILL'S NFL RETURN SEEMED IMMINENT AND THEN HIS DIVORCE TRIAL BEGAN WITH DOMESTIC ABUSE ALLEGATIONS Hill, 32, denied he ever punched Vaccaro's stomach while she was pregnant, twisted her breasts, pulled out her hair, shoved a lit blunt into her face, or left her on the side of a road – which Vaccaro claimed on the witness stand earlier this week. But Hill did admit to throwing Vaccaro up against a wall of their Sunny Isle, Florida condo, creating a hole in the structure. He did admit to threatening her by saying he knew people who could hurt her. And he did apologize for cursing out both Vaccaro and her mother – a rant that is on tape. That's not all. Hill accused Vaccaro of indirectly being responsible for causing the fire that burned down their home in Broward County. And he also accused her of causing him to play worse once they got married because of the constant fighting. "I felt like If you look at my career before and my career after I got married it was, like, trending down," he testified. "And it was, like, bad. I was like, man, am I really putting this product on the field? Do I really look that bad? It was hard." Hill's testimony wrapped up at 5:41 p.m. but he is scheduled back on the witness stand on Friday because Thursday's session was all direct testimony. Vaccaro's attorney will have a chance for redirect on Friday. So, a lot to unpack here. Hill and Vaccaro were married in November 2021, but there was no prenuptial or post-nuptial agreement. And that became one of the pillars of their constant fighting during the 18-month marriage. "Obviously, the postnup is definitely one of the constant arguments and then finances," Hill said. "I think that's a very important topic that has to be explored through this whole entire thing. "Then money getting stolen, and the mother of my kids. I would literally have conversations with the mothers of my [other] kids and she would be, 'You're doing, X, Y, Z with them. You're being intimate with them. "Those were the primary arguments." Hill admitted he and Vaccaro discussed the postnuptial seemingly countless times. And often those ended in arguments. Hill accused Vaccaro of marrying him because of her interest in his money. It began with Vaccaro taking $10,000 one time before their marriage. And then, he testified, the sums got larger after the marriage. "I was like, babe, why you stealing money?" Hill testified. "All you have to do is say, 'help me out.' She stole money then. She stole money during the marriage while getting what she was already getting, which she was getting $15K. "Then she was taking around $60K a month and I would see that and it'd be, 'You're giving this person this and that person that.'" Hill also said Vaccaro's monthly take at one point was $100,000 in one month. He also testified that Vaccaro didn't like his family around their baby girl. But when the couple's home burned, and they moved to the swank Porsche Design Tower in Miami, she moved her mom in. "It was one of those where I said have your mom come down for a little bit to help you out at the beginning of the pregnancy," Hill said. "I didn't know she was going to come down and stay for two years." The couple split but agreed to get counseling. During one of those sessions, Hill said, both agreed many of their conversations "were getting out of hand." That included allegations by Vaccaro that Hill was physically abusive on at least eight different times. Hill denied all those happened except one time he came home to pack clothes and leave. "As I'm getting my clothes, I feel somebody brush up behind me," Hill said. "And that person brushing up behind me is my wife, and I'm like, hold on, hold on ... That continued for like five minutes. "I told her don't you ever touch me again in your life. I pushed her against the wall. And I tried to force her to get off me. I created a hole in the wall, trying to force her to get off me that night." Hill testified that despite pushing his wife into a wall, he and her "got physically intimate that night." But later he had remorse and decided he definitely wanted a divorce. "I didn't want to be that in front of my daughter," he said. "I felt embarrassed, you know what I'm saying?" Hill also testified about a fateful car ride home in May 2024 in which Vaccaro claims he shoved her into a car door, threw her shoe out of the car and drank. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Hill admitted to drinking socially. And he also admitted he warned his wife about what might happen to her if he wanted to hurt her. "I did, I did make statements about she wasn't safe," Hill said. "I did make statements about me being able to get people to hurt her. Like now, looking back, I wish I could have handled that situation better. "I wish I could have talked to my wife better. I wish I could take it all back." Hill also testified that his grandmother and sister "wanted to do some things to [Vaccaro] but knew she was, in Hill's words, "the love of my life." articles.title: Guinness brewery that welcomed 2 million visitors closing its doors for good
articles.summary: One of America's two Guinness breweries is closing, leaving 174 Aramark employees out of work. The brewery's last day open to the public will be Nov. 1.
articles.body: The Guinness Open Gate Brewery in Halethorpe, Maryland, just outside Baltimore, will soon close, leaving the iconic Irish beer brand's Chicago brewery as its only U.S. location. Nov. 1 will mark the brewery's final day open to the public, leaving 174 Aramark employees out of work, according to a notice filed with the Maryland Department of Labor Oct. 1. The move comes amid a $1 billion restructuring plan at Diageo, Guinness' parent company. BREWERY THAT OFFERED FREE BEER WHEN TRUMP DIES FACES POSSIBLE CLOSURE AFTER STATE REVOKES ALCOHOL PERMITS Some teams at Diageo are losing 20% to 30% of their staff, Reuters reported in July. "This decision follows a careful review of our operations and long-term business priorities," a Diageo spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "It is not a reflection of the passion, talent or dedication of our team, nor of the support we have received from consumers and the Baltimore community since we opened our doors in 2018." Since opening in 2018, the Guinness Open Gate Brewery has welcomed more than 2 million visitors, according to a post on its Facebook page. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The brewery was the first to open in the U.S. since the Irish beer maker's previous brewery in New York closed in 1954, FOX Business reported at the time. "It's obviously a shame to see the Guinness brewery close in Maryland," said Derek Brown of Drink Company, a Washington, D.C.-based hospitality consulting and events company. "However, I'm not surprised in the sense that their core product remains Guinness, and now Guinness Zero," Brown told Fox News Digital. "The brewery focused on experimental products, which are interesting in themselves, but not necessarily primary drivers of Guinness' business." The experimental portion of the brewery allowed guests to concoct their own brews, and more than 700 beers were created over the years, according to the brewery's Facebook post. But changing trends in alcohol consumption likely played a role in the decision, industry experts say. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS New research shows that U.S. alcohol use has declined for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, Fox News Digital recently reported. More Americans are also alternating between alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages — a practice known as "zebra striping" — partly contributing to the decline, according to experts. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Our immediate focus is supporting affected colleagues through this transition," a Diageo spokesperson said. "We are committed to treating our team members with respect and providing resources and assistance to help them navigate the change." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The spokesperson added that Guinness "remains one of our most important brands, and we are committed to investing in its long-term growth and success. While our Baltimore brewery will close, our commitment to bringing Guinness to consumers around the world remains as strong as ever."

articles.title: Logan Federico’s dad says criminals have become 'more important' than victims, pushes repeat offender registry
articles.summary: Stephen Federico urged federal lawmakers to pass Logan's Law, a violent crime registry bill, at a South Carolina roundtable with AG Todd Blanche.
articles.body: The father of Logan Federico, a 22-year-old college student murdered during a home break-in, is demanding federal lawmakers close the legal loopholes that allow career criminals back onto the street. Stephen Federico is championing "Logan’s Law," a legislative proposal that would mandate a public database for repeat violent offenders, force cross-county and interstate communication, and hold prosecutors accountable when handling habitual criminals. The bill aims to eliminate systemic blind spots that allowed Logan's accused killer, Alexander Dickey, to avoid long-term confinement despite a lengthy record. ONE YEAR AFTER IRYNA ZARUTSKA MURDER, VIOLENT CRIMES FUEL NORTH CAROLINA PUBLIC SAFETY DEBATE "This was preventable. And d-----, I'm not going to save just one more life," Federico said Thursday during a South Carolina roundtable on crime reduction, which was attended by U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche. "I'm going to save thousands." Federico pointed to broader systemic breakdowns, comparing domestic criminal justice failures to immigration enforcement gaps. TEEN'S TRAGIC KILLING BY ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT BECOMES FLASHPOINT IN BATTLE FOR CONTROL OF CONGRESS "We are fighting 15 million that crossed our borders — some horrific criminals, some not," he added. "Now we're also fighting the constant felon. How are we supposed to win without Logan's Law?" Introduced by U.S. Rep. Russell Fry, R-S.C., and the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., Logan's Law has not yet formally come to the floor in either the House or the Senate. LINDSEY GRAHAM, SOUTH CAROLINA SENATOR WHO ROSE FROM SMALL-TOWN ROOTS TO GOP POWER BROKER, DIES AT 71 "Common sense works. Common sense is easy," Fry said, comparing the proposed legislation to existing public registries. "We have a sexual abuse registry that is publicly searchable. This is for violent crimes – it's the same concept." Attorney General Blanche urged lawmakers to move swiftly. "It took a tragedy to push it to the forefront," Blanche said. "But that's okay. I think the worst thing we could do is not act." Blanche expressed hope for bipartisan support, adding, "I don't think it's a controversial issue... I know President Trump supports it." BIDEN ADMIN RELEASED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF FATALLY STABBING FAIRFAX COUNTY MOTHER Logan Federico, a North Carolina college student, was staying with friends at a South Carolina home on May 3, 2025, when Dickey allegedly broke in. According to Columbia police, Dickey drove a stolen vehicle into the neighborhood, broke into one home to steal vehicle keys and a firearm, and then forced his way into the house where Federico was staying. Inside, Dickey stole credit cards and fatally shot Federico. Her father noted that she was awake during the intrusion. HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER "He didn't kill our daughter for a debit card," Federico said. "She was the only one awake who could identify him. He killed a witness." Dickey had an extensive criminal record dating back to 2013, including convictions for breaking and entering, burglary, grand larceny, strong-arm robbery, possession of a stolen vehicle, and resisting arrest. Critics and authorities argue he slipped through the cracks of a lenient justice system. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "What we do as a society right now is make the criminal more important than the innocent," Federico said, criticizing progressive policies such as reduced sentencing and no-cash bail. "We have turned the page. We are the underdogs." Fox News' David Spunt contributed to this report.

articles.title: KPSC scam candidates taken to resorts, provided with Q&A: ED

articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate on Thursday claimed that in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) paper leak case, candidates for the veterinary officers' exam were taken to resorts/Airbnb a day before the exam, provided test papers and their answer sheets, all for Rs 40 lakh per candidate.Two days ago, the agency had arrested KPSC ex-chairman Shivashankarappa and its member B V Geetha.Giving details of its investigation into alleged corruption in Karnataka PSC, the agency said Gyanendra Gangwar, the arrested IAS officer who was controller of examinations at KPSC, was in custody of confidential examination material and had leaked them to Geetha. The ED said an organised syndicate paid bribes to officials from top to bottom.The ED's probe by its Bengaluru unit is based on multiple FIRs registered by the police at Vidhana Soudha police station in the case of recruitment of 400 veterinary officers."Evidence gathered so far has revealed an organised mechanism for generation of proceeds of crime through manipulation of the KPSC recruitment process. KPSC officials leaked question papers and candidate specific answer keys," the ED added.ED searched the premises of former Shivashankarappa and Geetha on Oct 6, which was followed by their arrest."The searches resulted in seizure of blank signed cheques of Rs 80 lakh, along with blank signed promissory notes, from one of the successful candidates," the ED said. The agency has traced at least 10 successful candidates who were allegedly taken to a resort/Airbnb villa on the outskirts of Bengaluru a day before the examination, where they were provided with a question paper and correct answer options and made to practice/memorise them.According to the ED, the question paper (marked with correct answers) containing 80 questions was leaked by Gangwar through his close associate, Basavaraj Kannale, to these 10 candidates."Basavaraj Kannale has collected bribe money amounting to Rs 40-50 lakh from each candidate, in consideration of facilitating their final selection in the veterinary officers' recruitment exam," ED said.Gangwar and Kannale were arrested on Sept 17-18 and sent to ED custody for 14 days. "During ED custody, Gangwar disclosed crucial information relating to irregularities in conducting various KPSC recruitment exams," ED added.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
